item.title: ‘Power couple’ – Fans react to Caitlin Clark and Taylor Swift watching Chiefs game together
item.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images No two women in the United States can definitively say they are more famous than Taylor Swift and Caitlin Clark. So it stands to reason that those two getting together again has gone viral . The WNBA Finals may not involve Caitlin Clark, but she is still turning up at unexpected spots in the world of sports. The Indiana Fever superstar was recently seen taking in the Kansas City Chiefs game as they beat the Los Angeles Chargers comfortably on Sunday. Clark wasn’t there just by herself either, she was in the company of arguably the ‘First Lady’ of Chiefs Kingdom, Taylor Swift. The global superstar has become a regular fixture at games to support her husband, Travis Kelce, and she was once again doing so in Clark’s company. Worlds collide on social media as fans are thrilled to see Taylor Swift and Caitlin Clark together again The world of social media is in some ways made up of different corners. Swift’s fans, who love her music, occupy one of these corners. Fans of the WNBA and Clark, have their own corner too. However, it might just be safe to say that these two groups do have a reasonable amount of overlap. So when Swift and Clark were spotted together at Arrowhead once more, the reactions were quite excited and most of them were very positive, too. “Never thought I’d see Taylor and Caitlin in one frame, I love both of them so much,” one fan wrote. “POWER COUPLE. For real. The two of them together could change everything,” said another fan. “Two girls who happen to be the gold standard of their respective industries,” a third fan wrote. “Seeing those two hang out is not surprising at all, I love it,” a fourth fan added. “So nice to see Taylor supporting Travis, those two are the cutest. Adding CC to the equation just makes it so much better, too,” a different comment read. Swift and Clark both have their fair share of haters, but it is hard to be angry with them for simply enjoying a good game of football together. It will be interesting to see if they plan on attending any of the WNBA Finals games, although the reactions to that could end up being quite polarising. item.title: Carlos Baleba Could Change Manchester United’s Season
item.description: LEEDS, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Carlos Baleba of Manchester United during the players warm up ahead of the Premier League 2026/27 match between Leeds United and Manchester United at Elland Road on October 18, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Getty Images Manchester United is finding wins hard to come by at the moment. Indeed, Michael Carrick’s team is currently on a run of six matches in all competitions without a victory. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds United was the latest underwhelming performance and result by the Old Trafford outfit. There were, however, some positives for Carrick to pick out of the display, not least the performance of Carlos Baleba. In his first Premier League start as a Manchester United player, the Cameroonian was a commanding presence in central midfield, helping his new team on both sides of the ball. LEEDS, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Carlos Baleba of Manchester United controls the ball whilst under pressure from Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds United during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Leeds United and Manchester United at Elland Road on October 18, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Getty Images Carrick reshuffled his midfield unit for the trip to Elland Road, deploying Baleba and Andrey Santos at the base. This gave United a strong foundation to build from. Ahead of the pair, Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans were positioned in an advanced role where they could influence the attacking play in front of them. It was a midfield set up that gave Manchester United greater control of the match even if it still struggled to create good enough opportunities to find the back of the net. In Baleba, Carrick might finally have a two-way midfielder to build around with Santos also demonstrating his potential. “You look at the midfield with Manuel and Andey, that’s a pretty fresh spine of the team through the middle of the pitch,” said Carrick after the 1-1 draw. “And both young players are adapting to life at this football club, and I thought both of them were terrific today. I thought they both did really well in midweek, so that’s a massive positive for us.” Michael Carrick, manager of Manchester United, watches the Premier League match between Leeds United and Manchester United at Elland Road in Leeds, United Kingdom, on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images) NurPhoto via Getty Images This season has been a disappointing one for Manchester United to this point. The team is slumped in 12th place in the Premier League table and have won just one of its two Champions League fixtures so far. Carrick is fighting to prove he’s still the right man for the job at Old Trafford. And yet Baleba is offering some green shoots of progress. Carrick is still working out the right formula for success in the centre of the pitch, but Baleba is already showing why Manchester United was right to pay so much money to sign him from Brighton in

The challenging fixtures are coming thick and fast for Manchester United with Carrick and his players in Italy to face Como this week. After that, United will host Bournemouth before a tricky league game against Chelsea. With Baleba in the lineup, though, the outlook is slightly more positive. item.title: Shannon Sharpe claps back at callout from Travis Hunter’s wife Leanna Lenee
item.description: Another busy NFL Sunday kicked off bright and early for Week 6, with the Jacksonville Jaguars playing in their second consecutive game in London. The Jags failed to come away with a win, falling to the division rival Houston Texans on a last-second field goal, but there was one major bright spot. Former No. 2 overall pick Travis Hunter had a breakout performance on both sides of the ball, hauling in his first touchdown catch of the year before coming up with an interception late in the game. It was nearly enough to spark a Jacksonville comeback. After the game, Hunter’s wife, Leanna Lenee , was gloating about Hunter’s performance and took some time to call out some of his past critics who were outspoken with their thoughts that Hunter couldn’t be a two-way star as a pro. Specifically, Lenee aimed at Shannon Sharpe , who immediately clapped back on Nightcap with Chad “Ochocinco” Johnson on Sunday night. MORE: Travis Hunter’s wife Leanna Lenee rips Shannon Sharpe after TD/INT game Shannon Sharpe Responds To Public Callout From Leanna Lenee “Leanna, we appreciate you watching the show. We’ve never said anything bad about your husband, nor will we ever. Look, we talk about what we see. You’re talking about a couple of old ex-athletes that played their particular sports at very, very high levels. We know what good football is. We know what bad football is, and we don’t have a problem calling good and bad football out. That’s what we do. MORE: Travis Hunter shares rare NFL company with INT, TD reception in London game “All we said is that, hey, your husband is outstanding. He has All-Pro and Pro Bowl potential at the cornerback position. And if you use him situationally, he can be electric on the offensive side of the football. And today he showed it. She’s going to check you by her man. I ain’t got no problem with that. She’s supposed to stand. She’s supposed to be 10 toes down for it. Because I stand 10 toes down with my statement. Whatever I say, I stand on it.” Apr 24, 2025; Green Bay, WI, USA; Colorado Buffaloes wide receiver Travis Hunter with his mother Ferrante Harris and his fiancee Leanna Lenee on the red carpet before the 2025 NFL Draft at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) It doesn’t matter what side you take in this little debate; all that matters is Hunter showed he is capable of contributing on both sides of the ball at the highest level. His effort wasn’t enough for the team to get the win, but he made a statement with his performance. Hopefully, the Jaguars will find a way to continue using Hunter in ways that will help the team bring home the wins. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Takeaways from Maryland men’s basketball’s 90-81 exhibition win over West Virginia
item.description: Maryland men’s basketball unofficially kicked off basketball season in Xfinity Center Sunday, taking on local foes West Virginia in its second of three preseason games. The Terps started slowly, falling behind by as many as 19 points in the first half, before stringing together positive possessions after the break to complete the comeback with 10 minutes to go. From there, the teams went back and forth until an overtime period where the Terps kept the Mountaineers from making a field goal. Now, a behind-closed-doors scrimmage is all that separates the Terps from their official season opener on Nov. 2 against Bucknell. Here are three takeaways from Sunday’s matinee. Three-point shooting is still inconsistent Starting in his second consecutive preseason game, Boston University transfer Mike McNair Jr. took little time to make an impression on the home crowd. With the Terps recycling possession off an Andre Mills offensive rebound, McNair found a pocket of space beyond the arc. DJ Wagner found McNair, who shot over 44% from deep last season, and there was little doubt about what was coming next. McNair was brought in to be a 3-point specialist for head coach Buzz Williams, whose teams are often post-oriented and in need of marksmen that can drain 25-footers without much volume. The issue for Williams and Maryland is that it took 17 minutes after McNair opened the scoring for anyone else to make a 3-pointer. Maryland finished the afternoon 10-of-20 from beyond the arc, with McNair responsible for three of them. Mills, meanwhile, made four 3-pointers, including two in overtime to ice the game. Defending the 3-point shot appeared a concern for Maryland as well. The Terps frequently came unstuck with West Virginia’s switches in the first half, leaving an extra man open beyond the arc far too often. The Mountaineers made eight of their first 11 3-pointers, burying Maryland early. It was only when the visitors missed their next 14 from beyond the arc that the Terps were able to come back and force overtime. How much of that came down to Maryland’s defensive effort is up to interpretation. Pharrel Payne is still the team’s barometer Maryland will go as far as Pharrel Payne is able to take it. That was the case during the 2025-26 season, when Payne averaged 17.5 points and 7.2 rebounds per game in 10 games before getting injured in what became a lost season for the Terps. It remains the case ahead of the 2026-27 season, with Payne playing 37 of 45 minutes and finishing with 26 points and a game-high 13 rebounds. item.content:encoded: Maryland men’s basketball unofficially kicked off basketball season in Xfinity Center Sunday, taking on local foes West Virginia in its second of three preseason games. The Terps started slowly, falling behind by as many as 19 points in the first half, before stringing together positive possessions after the break to complete the comeback with 10 minutes to go. From there, the teams went back and forth until an overtime period where the Terps kept the Mountaineers from making a field goal. Now, a behind-closed-doors scrimmage is all that separates the Terps from their official season opener on Nov. 2 against Bucknell. Here are three takeaways from Sunday’s matinee. Three-point shooting is still inconsistent Starting in his second consecutive preseason game, Boston University transfer Mike McNair Jr. took little time to make an impression on the home crowd. With the Terps recycling possession off an Andre Mills offensive rebound, McNair found a pocket of space beyond the arc. DJ Wagner found McNair, who shot over 44% from deep last season, and there was little doubt about what was coming next. McNair was brought in to be a 3-point specialist for head coach Buzz Williams, whose teams are often post-oriented and in need of marksmen that can drain 25-footers without much volume. The issue for Williams and Maryland is that it took 17 minutes after McNair opened the scoring for anyone else to make a 3-pointer. Maryland finished the afternoon 10-of-20 from beyond the arc, with McNair responsible for three of them. Mills, meanwhile, made four 3-pointers, including two in overtime to ice the game. Defending the 3-point shot appeared a concern for Maryland as well. The Terps frequently came unstuck with West Virginia’s switches in the first half, leaving an extra man open beyond the arc far too often. The Mountaineers made eight of their first 11 3-pointers, burying Maryland early. It was only when the visitors missed their next 14 from beyond the arc that the Terps were able to come back and force overtime. How much of that came down to Maryland’s defensive effort is up to interpretation. Pharrel Payne is still the team’s barometer Maryland will go as far as Pharrel Payne is able to take it. That was the case during the 2025-26 season, when Payne averaged 17.5 points and 7.2 rebounds per game in 10 games before getting injured in what became a lost season for the Terps. It remains the case ahead of the 2026-27 season, with Payne playing 37 of 45 minutes and finishing with 26 points and a game-high 13 rebounds. It was Payne’s steady offensive boards that kept Maryland in the game, and it was his emphatic dunk off an alley-oop from Tomislav Buljan that slammed the door on West Virginia in overtime. “He brings so much attention offensively that everybody gets their opportunity,” Mills said. The big man is a critical component of the Maryland offense for his ability to make his teammates better — and occasionally bail them out, too. Baba Oladotun struggled to make inroads against West Virginia, and he dribbled himself into a corner with the Terps up a point midway through the second half. The shot clock raced towards zero as he shoveled a pass over the double-team to Payne. From 25 feet out, the big man struck nylon. “My response when he made the three was not, ‘can you believe that,’ because I’ve seen him work,” Williams said. “He’s just taking it to a completely different level.” Payne’s six turnovers and his 5-of-11 shooting from the free-throw line are both parts of his game that need to be ironed out. However, a big afternoon in his first game back in College Park is a promising sign for the season ahead. Maryland is still resilient While it was only an exhibition game, Maryland’s response following halftime is a sign that the team is willing to fight through hardship. While last year’s Terps finished with their worst record in over 80 years, they displayed an ability late in the season to stay resilient and find a way to win. With massive roster turnover, this was the first opportunity for Williams to determine whether this year’s Terps team — which is on pace to perform far better — had the same traits. “He was really just asking us, like, what’s our, what’s going to be our response,” McNair said. “How do we respond to adversity? Do we back down? Are we going to fight back? Just, just who are we as a team? Where are we as a group?” The Terps answered those questions with a ferocious effort early in the second half. “We had energy in the first half, but like we came out [of halftime] with even more. We focused on the details even more,” Mills said. “I think that from the first half to the second half, it was like night and day for sure.” Against a physical team that is also projected to finish around the NCAA tournament bubble, Maryland found a way. As the Terps continue to gel, they can take comfort in knowing that they have the ability to turn games around — an ability that could prove to make the difference in March.

item.title: Spalletti responds to Bremer after Juventus 0-3 Lazio: ‘Have to look at ourselves’
item.description: Spalletti responds to Bremer after Juventus 0-3 Lazio: ‘Have to look at ourselves’ Luciano Spalletti said that Juventus players need to look at themselves after Gleison Bremer criticised his teammates for not showing enough character in Sunday’s 3-0 Serie A defeat against Lazio, but says that he will be doing the same of himself: ‘I need to ask myself questions and find the answers’. What Spalletti said after Bremer’s criticism of Juventus The tension is palpable in Juventus circles following Sunday’s 3-0 defeat at home against Lazio, which has left the Bianconeri eight points off the league leaders after just seven matches. They are currently worse off in terms of points than they were at the same stage of the 2025-26 season, just before Igor Tudor was dismissed from his position as head coach. TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Oliver Provstgaard Nielsen of SS Lazio scores the opening goal during the Serie A match between Juventus and SS Lazio at Allianz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) It was a miserable evening for Juventus supporters, some of whom turned on each other and began fighting in the stands . They were heavily criticised in Monday morning’s newspapers and defender Bremer also chastised his teammates , claiming ‘I can’t carry everyone’. “It is true, the coach gives indications, but we are the ones who need to put it into action on the field,” said the Juventus defender after full-time on Sunday. “However, there are 11 players on the field, plus the five who come off the bench, so I cannot just carry everyone. I try to give a hand, I talk to them, but they all have their own character. We can push them to a certain point, but that’s all, some have more character than others.” TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Luciano Spalletti, Manager of Juventus, looks on before the Serie A match between Juventus and Atalanta BC at Allianz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Spalletti was asked for his response to Bremer’s remarks in an interview with Sky Sport Italia shortly afterwards. The coach said: “He needs to give a response, it’s good that he does his analysis. He’s as much a part of today’s game as I was, whether I’m in the stands or on the touchline, I’m involved too. “Before talking about the team, we have to look at ourselves as individuals. In my own analysis, looking at the way things were managed and the journey that led to tonight’s performance, I need to examine myself. I need to ask myself questions and find the answers, otherwise it becomes too easy to just shift the blame onto others.”

item.title: Kentucky Wildcats News: Vanderbilt and Texas Tech Game Week
item.description: This past weekend marked our first UK basketball/football doubleheader, and now we’re preparing for another with two games in Lexington this coming weekend for the Kentucky Wildcats . On Friday, Mark Pope’s Wildcats will face a stiff pre-season test, as the Texas Tech Red Raiders come to town. The Red Raiders are projected to be a top-25 team to start the season, but they currently face eligibility questions regarding some key players, including returners Darrion Williams and Donovan Atwell, as well as UCF transfer JaMichael Stillwell. Star forward JT Toppin is also out this week as he continues to recover from a torn ACL that will likely keep him out until sometime in conference play. Regardless, Texas Tech under Grant McCasland has been solid and should be a good measuring stick to see where this Kentucky team stands heading into the season. Meanwhile, Kentucky Football returns home for an SEC matchup against Vanderbilt in front of what was recently announced as a sold-out crowd at Kroger Field. While Vanderbilt has struggled this season, currently sitting at 3-4, this isn’t a game the Wildcats can overlook. Vanderbilt has won three of the last four matchups between these two teams, and after losing four straight in SEC play, the Commodores will be desperate for a win on Saturday. We’re set up for another big week in Lexington. Go Cats! item.title: The Packers’ defense delivered the answer Dallas needed to see
item.description: The Packers’ defense delivered the answer Dallas needed to see originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys entered Sunday night hoping a players-only meeting and a new defensive voice would help turn the season around. Instead, Green Bay’s defense delivered the most convincing response of the night. The Packers intercepted Dak Prescott twice and held Dallas to 13 points in a 23-13 victory at Lambeau Field. The Cowboys entered the game averaging 27.6 points per game, but they went into halftime trailing 17-0 and could not make up the difference. Green Bay improved to 4-2 with its third straight win. Dallas fell to 2-4, and the loss extended a frustrating stretch for a team that had hoped to find a spark after its Week 5 defeat. Turnovers changed the game Prescott’s two interceptions halted promising Dallas possessions. Evan Williams picked him off in the second quarter, and rookie Brandon Cisse recorded the first interception of his career later in the half. Mess with the Bull.... 📺: NBC https://t.co/1OLoZa8Hig — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 19, 2026 Green Bay turned the second takeaway into points. Jordan Love scored on a 1-yard run with 23 seconds remaining before halftime, giving the Packers a 17-0 advantage. The Cowboys had been shut out in the first half for the first time since 2021. Love finished with 276 passing yards, a touchdown pass and a rushing score. Matthew Golden caught six passes for 104 yards and a touchdown, giving the Packers an early lead they never surrendered. MORE : Browns’ defense flips the script as Cleveland stuns Ravens Dallas showed one sign of progress The Cowboys’ defense did produce two takeaways of its own, including Dallas’ first interception of the season. The unit also kept the final margin from growing after Green Bay’s early control. That progress may matter, but it was not enough to overcome the slow start. Dallas was still limited to 13 points, and its offense did not find the end zone until late in the fourth quarter. The Cowboys have another difficult test coming: a road matchup with Philadelphia on Oct. 26. Green Bay heads to Detroit next Sunday. The Packers leave Week 6 with a strong defensive result, while Dallas has to turn its meeting-room changes into better play on the field. More NFL news: Joey Porter Jr. news considered ‘good’ after Steelers trade JJ McCarthy gets major starting job prediction despite New York’s 3-1 start Vikings get positive Justin Jefferson update after making wise decision against Dolphins

item.title: German tennis great Kerber to be honoured as 'Legend of Sport'
item.description: Former tennis player Angelique Kerber speaks at a press conference for the 44th German Sports Press Ball. Kerber will be honoured as a 'Sports Legend' at the event, which takes place at the Alte Oper in Frankfurt am Main, on 7 November 2026. (is associated with: «German tennis great Kerber to be honoured as 'Legend of Sport'») Florian Wiegand/dpa German tennis great Angelique Kerber will be honoured as a "Legend of Sport" at the Sports Press Ball in Frankfurt on November 7. She joins a list of renowned athletes such as seven-time Formula One champion Michael Schumacher, football World Cup winners Franz Beckenbauer, Lothar Matthäus, Rudi Völler, and former tennis player Boris Becker, among others. "I don’t feel that old yet. But this award means a great deal to me. It’s a great honour," the 38-year-old said. "I always wanted to be seen as an athlete who gave her all and left her heart on the court. I think I’ve achieved that. I’ve achieved all my dreams. It couldn’t be better," she said in a news conference on Monday. During her active career, Kerber won three Grand Slams and held the top spot in the women's ranking for 34 weeks.

item.title: Travis Hunter made NFL history, but the Jaguars still left London with a loss
item.description: Travis Hunter made NFL history, but the Jaguars still left London with a loss originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Travis Hunter produced the kind of two-way performance Jacksonville hoped to see when it selected him second overall in the 2025 NFL Draft. The Jaguars still lost, but Hunter’s day in London was historic. Hunter caught a 7-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence early in the fourth quarter, then intercepted Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud in the end zone on the Texans ’ next drive. He became the first NFL player since Brian Dawkins in 2002 to record both a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game. The Jaguars ultimately fell 34-31 when Houston kicker Ka’imi Fairbairn made a 49-yard field goal as time expired. Hunter’s rare contribution helped Jacksonville stay within reach, but the Texans got the final points. Hunter made an impact on both sides Hunter finished with four catches for 59 yards and the touchdown. His interception was his second of the season and came with Houston threatening to extend its lead. TRAVIS HUNTER TOUCHDOWN! HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/UEbQwJYHqy — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 The sequence showed why Jacksonville wants Hunter involved on both sides of the ball. His touchdown pulled the Jaguars within three early in the fourth quarter. When Houston drove back into scoring range, Hunter’s end-zone interception gave Jacksonville another chance to take control. That kind of impact is unusual even for a player with Hunter’s college résumé. He won the 2024 Heisman Trophy at Colorado while playing both receiver and cornerback, and Sunday offered an NFL example of that rare versatility. MORE : C.J. Stroud’s fourth-quarter comeback kept the Texans alive against Jacksonville A milestone won’t erase the missed opportunity Jacksonville will have mixed feelings about the result. Hunter delivered a memorable performance, and the Jaguars had a chance to win another close game in London. Instead, Fairbairn’s kick ended the afternoon with Houston celebrating. The loss also snapped Jacksonville’s three-game winning streak. Hunter’s effort gives the team something to build on, but the Jaguars need to turn standout individual moments into wins. For Hunter, Sunday’s achievement is a major marker in his young career. For Jacksonville, it is also a reminder that even a historic performance needs a finish to become a victory. item.title: Off-Script Ohio: Ohio State survives Indiana, but loses Julian Sayin
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes catches a pass for a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ugly, ugly, ugly. But a win is a win, and this one ended Indiana’s 22-game winning streak and avenged last December. Ohio State’s first drive stalled in a field goal, and the next ended with a Julian Sayin interception that set up a quick Indiana touchdown. The Buckeyes took a 10-7 lead into halftime when Sayin found Bo Jackson for a touchdown on fourth-and-goal. Early in the fourth quarter, Sayin hit a double covered Jeremiah Smith for a 38-yard touchdown on fourth-and-1 to make it 19-7. That was Smith’s 39th career touchdown catch, tying Braylon Edwards’ Big Ten record. Then Indiana stormed back with a touchdown and a two-point conversion to make it 19-15. With Sayin hurt, Luke Fahey couldn’t move the ball, and the Hoosiers got it right back. They appeared to score the go-ahead touchdown on fourth down with a minute left, but Nick Marsh’s left foot came down out of bounds, and Ohio State escaped Bloomington with a win. Takeaways The defense is back. Indiana came in averaging 221 rushing yards a game and finished with just 73. The defensive line was dominant against the run, the Buckeyes forced two fumbles, and Jay Timmons was excellent in his return. Sayin struggled before getting hurt. He threw two touchdowns, but he also threw two interceptions, missed throws and never looked comfortable against Indiana’s pass rush. Then Mario Landino sacked him in the fourth quarter, and Ryan Day said afterward that he’ll “probably be out several weeks.” Fahey went 0-for-2 in relief and now likely takes over as the starter. Indiana’s kicking game ended up being the thing that decided it. Nico Radicic missed field goals from 32 and 55 yards in a four-point game. Season outlook The bye week comes at the right time, giving Fahey and Tavien St. Clair each a chance with the first team and Sayin extra time to heal. After that, the schedule is at USC, Oregon, Northwestern, at Nebraska and Michigan. At 6-1, Ohio State is in good shape and probably has room for one or maybe even two more losses to still make the playoff, but USC on the road and Oregon at home with a freshman quarterback will be tough. The defense and run game will need to carry more of the load until Sayin returns. Around college football For the first time ever, five of the top seven teams lost in the same weekend: Auburn 27, No. 1 Georgia 24 No. 8 BYU 28, No. 3 Notre Dame 24 No. 14 Tennessee 26, No. 6 Alabama 10 Florida 27, No. 7 Texas 24 Miami also needed double overtime to survive, Ole Miss beat Missouri by 30, and Kentucky, Utah and UCLA all kept rolling. It was one of the craziest weekends in recent memory, and Ohio State moved up to No. 3 in the AP Poll as a result.

At 6-1, Ohio State is in good shape and probably has room for one or maybe even two more losses to still make the playoff, but USC on the road and Oregon at home with a freshman quarterback will be tough. The defense and run game will need to carry more of the load until Sayin returns. Around college football For the first time ever, five of the top seven teams lost in the same weekend: Auburn 27, No. 1 Georgia 24 No. 8 BYU 28, No. 3 Notre Dame 24 No. 14 Tennessee 26, No. 6 Alabama 10 Florida 27, No. 7 Texas 24 Miami also needed double overtime to survive, Ole Miss beat Missouri by 30, and Kentucky, Utah and UCLA all kept rolling. It was one of the craziest weekends in recent memory, and Ohio State moved up to No. 3 in the AP Poll as a result.

item.title: Drew Mestemaker 'can’t do those dumb plays' if OSU football wants to make noise | Carlson
item.description: HOUSTON — Drew Mestemaker hoped for one more chance, but standing on the Oklahoma State sideline Saturday night at Houston , the Cowboy quarterback knew he didn’t get to determine whether he and the offense would get it. The defense had to get a stop in the final minutes of the game. Mestemaker felt helpless watching. “But then,” he said, “you also got to look back.” Back at what the offense had done. And not done. On a night Houston defeated OSU 35-32 , there was plenty of blame to go around for the Cowboys. The defense struggled to tackle, contain receivers in the secondary and get off the field on third- and fourth-down. The coaches have identified that slow starts are a huge and ongoing problem, but they have yet to identify a fix. More: Can Oklahoma State football fix secondary problems that Conner Weigman, Houston exposed? Still, the harsh reality is that Mestemaker and the offense didn’t do enough. They scored only three points in the first half. Managed just 14 rushing yards before halftime. Turned the ball over twice. Both of those turnovers were Mestemaker’s, an interception and a fumble. He fumbled another time, too, but the Cowboys recovered it. Those kinds of miscues are difficult to overcome, especially when the quarterback on the other sideline is clicking — and Cougar quarterback Conner Weigman was doing just that. They scored only three points in the first half. Managed just 14 rushing yards before halftime. Turned the ball over twice. Both of those turnovers were Mestemaker’s, an interception and a fumble. Now, Weigman is no stiff. Morris, who knows a good quarterback when he sees one, held Weigman in high regard long before Saturday night’s game. “I just think he’s improved so drastically over the course of the last year and a half and is really comfortable in this offense,” Morris said. “Great player.” But Mestemaker has played so well over the past month or so that it seemed unlikely that he wouldn’t be the best quarterback on the field. But when he had chances to make plays, he missed on a few too many. On OSU’s first possession, the Cowboys had a third-and-goal from the 5, and Mestemaker just missed connecting with Wyatt Young. OSU settled for a field goal, which didn’t seem all that bad. But on the Cowboys’ next possession, Mestemaker again had a couple of shots into the end zone that didn’t connect. A first-down throw to Justin Bowick from the Cougar 23-yard line. A fourth-down throw to Young from the 2. Neither hit. More: Oklahoma State football QB Drew Mestemaker not good enough vs Houston | Report card And failing on fourth down meant no points. On the first two drives of the game, OSU got within 5 yards of the end zone both times and managed only three points. That’s a kick in the teeth. “We can't be a team that can't score in the red zone, an offense that is a one-half team,” Mestemaker said. “We have to play a full game on offense, and it starts with me. I have to play better at the end of the day." Granted, Mestemaker was 22 of 34 for 365 yards and three touchdowns. He also ran for 34 yards on six carries. But his turnovers and misses early narrowed the Cowboys’ path to victory — and ultimately, it dead-ended. “I just can’t do those dumb plays,” Mestemaker said, “and give our defense some short fields.” Morris didn’t lay all the blame at Mestemaker’s feet. “I thought he was getting pressure; early on, they did a nice job with some twist game, and they hit us with some zero blitzes at times,” Morris said. “Receiver missed the hot route; (Mestemaker) had nowhere to go with it.” But … “Probably not his best performance.” Definitely uneven. First half: 6 of 15 for 124 yards, no touchdowns, one interception. Second half: 16 of 19 for 241 yards, three touchdowns, no interceptions. More: Exclusive: Who is Rick Sosa and why does he want to help Oklahoma State athletics? Mestemaker was a big reason why the Cowboys had to play from behind, but at the same time, he was a big reason why they almost came from behind to knock off the Cougars. On OSU’s final possession, Mestemaker was 6 for 6 on an array of throws, hitting tight end Carson Kolb over the middle, shoveling a pass to Ayo Adeyi, finding Young for a couple of 17-yard gains, connecting with Chris Barnes for a short gain, then finding Bowick in the left corner of the end zone for the touchdown that drew the Cowboys to within three points. Mestemaker even threw in a nifty 29-yard dash down the sideline that got the Cowboys into the red zone. “He’s maybe the toughest kid on our team,” Morris said. “He continued to battle. His competitive character is through the roof. “Gave us a chance at the end.” But of course, Mestemaker and the rest of the offense were left to hope that the defense would get them one more opportunity. If only they’d taken advantage of the opportunities when they had them earlier in the game. “Obviously, you want the ball in that last second,” Mestemaker said. “But I'm not blaming the defense in that moment. “I’m not one to point fingers.” After all, there's the bit about how if you point one finger, three others are pointing back at you. But on Saturday night, that’s the kind of scrutiny Mestemaker and the OSU offense deserved. Jenni Carlson: Jenni can be reached at jcarlson@oklahoman.com. Like her at facebook.com/JenniCarlsonOK, follow her at @jennicarlsonok.bsky.social and twitter.com/jennicarlson_ok, and support her work and that of other Oklahoman journalists by purchasing a digital subscription today. item.title: What Dink Pate's exit means for Providence basketball this season
item.description: PROVIDENCE – Two chapters were closed on this Providence men’s basketball season Saturday afternoon. The Friars played publicly for the first time, cruising past Pittsburgh in an exhibition at Amica Mutual Pavilion. They also suited up without Dink Pate, who will pursue a return to professional basketball after spending the last six months committed to Providence. Pate wasn’t on the bench for this 87-64 thumping of the Panthers . Friars coach Bryan Hodgson confirmed on social media Friday the athletic wing would leave the program and explore finding a place in the same NBA G League where he spent the last three years. “We signed Dink with the expectation that he would be able to play this year,” Hodgson said during his postgame press conference. “There was guidance and rules passed afterwards that changed those expectations. We fought through some of them. “It got to this point where we’re sitting here in the middle of October, push came to shove, and Dink had to make a decision. We fully support him in that decision.” Pate was looking at a Monday deadline to sign an Exhibit 10 deal, the same type of contract he agreed to last season with the Westchester Knicks. Pate played 36 games with Westchester, the affiliate of the defending NBA champion New York Knicks , before making an April pledge to Providence. He practiced with the team throughout the summer sessions and was with them through the preseason this fall. “ Every day he came in with positive energy even though he knew he was facing a lot of stuff behind the scenes,” Providence guard Malik Mack said. “He was a tremendous teammate. Great guy.” Pate was facing both academic and professional eligibility questions from the NCAA, which had yet to clear Pate for competition. The Friars were still trading paperwork with the sport’s governing body, and Pate wasn’t guaranteed a chance to take the floor in 2026-27 or beyond. He had yet to start collecting on whatever financial arrangement he made with Providence for the upcoming season. “Nobody gets paid by Providence College or (name, image and likeness) or (revenue) share until they’re fully certified and able to check into a basketball game,” Hodgson said. “That’s the bottom line. That’s with anything. “There’s this misconception out there that Dink made a bunch of money for a couple months and now he’s out of here. That’s not the case. If anything, Dink brought us a lot of value for the time he was on campus. He's a phenomenal young man.” Providence impressed on the perimeter in this one even without Pate’s services. The Friars dished out 22 assists and connected 15 times from 3-point range – they exceeded that assist number only twice last year and didn’t make more shots from deep in a single game. We fully support him in that decision.” Pate was looking at a Monday deadline to sign an Exhibit 10 deal, the same type of contract he agreed to last season with the Westchester Knicks. Great guy.” Pate was facing both academic and professional eligibility questions from the NCAA, which had yet to clear Pate for competition. If anything, Dink brought us a lot of value for the time he was on campus. He's a phenomenal young man.” Providence impressed on the perimeter in this one even without Pate’s services. The Friars dished out 22 assists and connected 15 times from 3-point range – they exceeded that assist number only twice last year and didn’t make more shots from deep in a single game. Miles Byrd led all scorers with 17 points, Ryan Mela chipped in 15 and the point guard duo of Malik Mack and Gavin Hightower each finished with seven assists. “Anybody who watched our exhibition game today would probably tell you this team wasn’t built around one guy who wasn’t here today,” Hodgson said. “It was pretty evident today. “Is Dink a good basketball player? Absolutely. But we did not build this roster around one guy. Losing Dink Pate hurts us more as human beings than it does as a basketball team, transparently. “This team is going to be just fine without Dink.” Providence was also without guards Devin Vanterpool (left ankle) and Ryan Sabol (left shoulder) due to injury and potential fifth-year additions Derek Simpson and Joseph Pinion due to their pending legal case. Simpson and Pinion have a virtual hearing Monday morning with the Rhode Island branch of U.S. District Court, and they’re seeking both injunctive relief and a temporary restraining order alongside a federal antitrust lawsuit. “We’ve got Dink’s back no matter what,” Byrd said. “His next decision is up to him, but we’re going to be his brothers for the rest of our lives. We built that.” bkoch@providencejournal.com On X: @BillKoch25 This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: What Dink Pate's exit means for Providence basketball this season

item.title: Amari Whiting brings her veteran presence to Iowa women's basketball
item.description: IOWA CITY — Amari Whiting joined Iowa women's basketball as a transfer in the offseason, and one of the most valuable things she brings to the Hawkeyes roster is how long she has been playing college basketball. After being Idaho's girls basketball Gatorade Player of the Year in 2022, her senior year of high school, Whiting went on to play for BYU. She played for the Cougars her freshman and sophomore seasons, starting in all 63 games of her career there. Whiting then transferred to Oklahoma State for her third year of college hoops, starting the next 34. Keeping track? Before even stepping foot on the court in an Iowa uniform, Whiting has logged 97 career games at the Division I power-conference level. "I do feel like I'm a vet in as far as I've played a lot of basketball in my life," Whiting said at Iowa women's basketball's media day on Oct. 13. "But at the same time, I kind of get giddy like a freshman again. I'm learning all these new things, and everything's been great. I'm just excited to bring my IQ in places that are needed, but also just learn." Amari Whiting is excited to play in front of Hawkeye fans When Whiting signed with Iowa in April , head coach Jan Jensen noted that her basketball IQ and her defense were two of the things in her game that the Hawkeyes were excited to have. With four transfer players on the roster this year (Whiting, Bria Medina, Dani Carnegie and Jocelyn Faison), Jensen said that the winning culture of Iowa and the fan base are a few things that were attractive to this year's transfer class. "I think that they want to win," Jensen said in her press conference at media day on Oct. 13. "They are bought into winning. They're bought into how Iowa has won. That was attractive. And certainly being part of this incredible fan base... I think that was part of the reason for these four to come in. It's fun to play here. It's meaningful to play here. It's special to play here." Whiting has 101,000 followers on Instagram , posting videos with her teammates that range from vlogging a gear haul to dancing and joking around. Once she announced her commitment to Iowa, she said lots of fans were reaching out, excited to welcome her. "I have a lot of fun with social media," Whiting said. "Once I committed, and even when I was on campus, I got a lot of Iowa followers. I get lots of DMs and comments of just like, 'Hey, we're excited to have you play here, and just excited for the season.'" What Amari Whiting brings to the Hawkeyes Whiting, a guard, takes pride in her defense. Her 1.76 steals per game last season ranked among the top 15 in the Big 12. She averaged 5.82 rebounds, 16th in the Big 12. "I'm just the kind of girl that likes to get it done defensively, and then I kind of let my offense come to me," Whiting said. "I'll just be aggressive when it's needed and just kind of lock down on D." She has a lot of goals and expectations this year, but one of the main ones is to have a long season, and go deep into the NCAA Tournam

item.title: McLaren set to decide Lando Norris punishment in Austin: What happened the last time
item.description: McLaren still have not said whether Lando Norris will face internal consequences for taking Oscar Piastri out of the Singapore Sprint, as the flashpoint will spark conversation in Austin as to whether the Brit should be penalised. The stewards took no action over the final-lap contact at Turn 5 and declared that "both drivers had contributed to the incident." Piastri retired, while Norris carried on to finish eighth. That gave McLaren a single point instead of the nine it would have scored for fourth and fifth, that could cost them millions in prize money . Andrea Stella has made clear the matter is not closed at McLaren and told reporters that apologies alone cannot fix it. The team planned further talks during the week off before the next triple-header begins in Austin this week. Photo: FOM Photo: FOM How McLaren punished Norris in 2025 There is a clear template to how McLaren should proceed. At the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix, Norris passed Piastri for third on lap one by going down the inside of Turn 3 and banging wheels with his teammate. Piastri asked the team to swap the cars back, but McLaren refused. The consequences only came out two weeks later. On the Thursday in Austin, Norris surprised the paddock by revealing he would face "repercussions" that could affect him until the end of the season. Zak Brown , who has been left red faced by the latest coming together , played the punishment down and would not say what it was. It was a pretty minor situation, so it's a pretty minor consequence. Brown told Sky Sports F1 the sanction would be "marginal" and that the team would have "zero interference" on a grand prix Sunday, and that the consequences were understood to be sporting ones. They were believed to be allowing Piastri choose whether to leave the garage before or after Norris in the final part of qualifying, and that this was meant to last for the rest of the season. Sanction gone within half a weekend The penalty barely got going. At the start of the 2025 Austin Sprint, Piastri turned into Nico Hülkenberg's Sauber at the first corner and then crashed into Norris, taking both McLarens out. After reviewing the crash, the team wiped the slate clean. "The consequences on Lando's side have been removed," Piastri confirmed before the Mexico City Grand Prix. Norris never said what the sanction had been, but he admitted it had hurt him. It was certainly a disadvantage. I would never choose it. Why Austin 2026 is different Singapore was the sixth and final Sprint weekend of the 2026 season while the United States Grand Prix this weekend follows the traditional format: three practice sessions, qualifying on Saturday and the race on Sunday 25 October. If McLaren use the same tool again, the first test would come straight away in Saturday qualifying. There would be no Sprint beforehand that could produce a reversal like last year's. After Austin come Mexico on 1 November, São Paulo on 8 November, then Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. The stakes have

item.title: Bengals Bye Week Awards: Team MVP
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals hit the bye at 3-2, and if you squint, you can see how this team could’ve been 5-0 or 1-4. A three-point loss in Pittsburgh. A five-point loss to Jacksonville after Ja’Marr Chase left with a concussion in the first 18 minutes. Then a 31-24 win in Miami to stop the bleeding. So who’s been the one player this team can’t do without? Here are the nominees. Joe Burrow, QB : 135-of-189 (71.4%), 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns, three interceptions, and a 104.4 passer rating. That completion percentage leads the NFL. He’s done it while losing Colbie Young on the first play in Pittsburgh, Chase early against Jacksonville, and Tee Higgins late in that same game. Four touchdowns in Miami went to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, Tanner Hudson and Chase. That’s an MVP spreading the wealth. Tee Higgins, WR : 27 catches for a team-high 423 yards (15.7 per catch). When Chase was out or limited, Higgins was the guy keeping defenses honest down the field. Ja’Marr Chase, WR: While Chase had a quiet debut and battled a concussion against the Jaguars, he has had his share of splash plays. He has four receiving touchdowns through five games, and continues to be a key to the Bengals’ success. Boye Mafe, DE : The biggest free-agent deal of the offseason, and he’s earned it: three sacks, five tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He’s been among the league leaders in pressures, and he tipped the pass that became Battle’s first interception in Miami. Dexter Lawrence II, DT: The biggest free agent acquisition (figuratively and literally) by the Bengals has had a big impact on the previously maligned defense. Through five games, Lawrence has three sacks, nine tackles (five for loss), and eats up space for other defenders. Is it fair that a quarterback almost always wins this? If Burrow weren’t eligible, who’s your MVP? Sound off on the comments!

A five-point loss to Jacksonville after Ja’Marr Chase left with a concussion in the first 18 minutes. Then a 31-24 win in Miami to stop the bleeding. That completion percentage leads the NFL. He’s done it while losing Colbie Young on the first play in Pittsburgh, Chase early against Jacksonville, and Tee Higgins late in that same game. Four touchdowns in Miami went to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, Tanner Hudson and Chase. That’s an MVP spreading the wealth. Tee Higgins, WR : 27 catches for a team-high 423 yards (15.7 per catch). When Chase was out or limited, Higgins was the guy keeping defenses honest down the field. Ja’Marr Chase, WR: While Chase had a quiet debut and battled a concussion against the Jaguars, he has had his share of splash plays. He has four receiving touchdowns through five games, and continues to be a key to the Bengals’ success. Boye Mafe, DE : The biggest free-agent deal of the offseason, and he’s earned it: three sacks, five tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He’s been among the league leaders in pressures, and he tipped the pass that became Battle’s first interception in Miami. Dexter Lawrence II, DT: The biggest free agent acquisition (figuratively and literally) by the Bengals has had a big impact on the previously maligned defense. Through five games, Lawrence has three sacks, nine tackles (five for loss), and eats up space for other defenders. Is it fair that a quarterback almost always wins this? If Burrow weren’t eligible, who’s your MVP? Sound off on the comments!

item.title: WNBA Finals hero Gabby Williams makes surprise Warriors appearance as NBA shares special moment
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images Gabby Williams was among the many fans present at the Golden State Warriors’ open practice on Sunday, October 18 at Chase Center. The Golden State Valkyries star had led her team to a win in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals just a day before at Chase Center, which is called the Ballhalla when the Valkyries play. Williams scored 26 points, 16 of which came in the second quarter. With the Atlanta Dream keeping the game close until the very end, the Valkyries needed Williams to make clutch free throws to secure their win. She showed great composure and made the last two shots from the charity stripe with 4 seconds left to play, leading to a 68-64 win for the home team. With the next game scheduled on Monday, Williams decided to wind down a little and stay close to the court to keep herself motivated. Gabby Williams shows up at Golden State Warriors open practice Sitting in the front row to see the Warriors practice, Williams was greeted by veteran Gary Payton II. The Warriors players have been extremely supportive of the Valkyries, with a few even going to Game 1 and cheering for the players. With the Warriors expected to start their season only on Thursday, players on the team could return the favour once again and support Williams and her teammates for Game 2. The team will once again hope for a big performance from Williams, as she is the player who helps get the best out of her teammates. While she went on to score 26 in Game 1, no other player added double figures, which shows that the team is reliant on her to produce on the offensive end while being the anchor on defence. Williams has had no problem fulfilling this role for the team and with a packed Ballhalla Arena cheering on for her, she will certainly take the task of helping the Valkyries to a 2-0 lead seriously. item.title: Sonay Kartal posts message on social media after losing Wuhan Open final to Maja Chwalinska
item.description: Sonay Kartal’s dreams of becoming a WTA 1000 champion were ended on Sunday evening following defeat in the Wuhan Open final. Despite being ranked 170th on the Tour, Kartal marched into the Chinese WTA 1000 final, defeating Belinda Bencic, Elina Svitolina, Jasmine Paolini and Jelena Ostapenko en route. Maja Chwalinska, from Poland, defeated Kartal in the final , 2-6, 6-4, 6-2. Following Sunday’s contest, Kartal posted a short message on social media. Sonay Kartal’s message after losing the Wuhan Open final “Leaving China with my head held high,” Kartal, who has risen 121 places in the WTA rankings to world number 49, said in an Instagram post on Sunday. Sonay Kartal’s Wuhan Open campaign R1: defeated Anhelina Kalinina 7-5, 6-3 R2: defeated Belinda Bencic 6-0, 7-5 R3: defeated Jasmine Paolini 6-2, 6-0 Quarter-finals: defeated Elina Svitolina 6-2, 2-6, 6-4 Semi-finals: defeated Jelena Ostapenko 7-6, 7-6 Final: lost to Maja Chwalinska 6-2, 4-6, 2-6 “The support has been incredible, so thank you,” the British star concluded. Kartal also posted an image on her Instagram story, depicting herself with the runner’s-up trophy and her team. “So special having these three people with me these past few weeks,” Kartal said. “The ones who got me back to being healthy. The ones who got me back to competing. “And the ones who deserve this moment.” Kartal can walk away from Wuhan with her head held high, despite losing Sunday’s final; few would have expected the British star to advance as far as she did upon the tournament’s commencement last week. Maja Chwalinska has also confirmed her status as one of the most exciting breakout players of the 2026 season. The Polish star, who has risen 11 places to world number 11 following her performances in China, also reached the Roland Garros final earlier this year. Both Kartal and Chwalinska have withdrawn from WTA events after competing in the Wuhan Open final: Kartal withdrew from the Osaka Open while Chwalinska withdrew from the Ningbo Open. Kartal has cited a right knee injury as the reason for her withdrawal, while Chwalinska has cited a left thigh injury. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Sonay Kartal is the new British number one Kartal has now achieved one of her main goals as a tennis player by attaining the status of British number one. The Sidcup-born player has overtaken Katie Boulter, Fran Jones, Harriet Dart and Emma Raducanu in the rankings. Sonay Kartal – 49 Katie Boulter – 58 Fran Jones – 99 Emma Raducanu – 109 Harriet Dart – 117 Kartal has become the fourth British number one since 2020 and 24th since 1975. “There are a lot of things that I want to achieve in my career and that [becoming British number one] was up there,” Kartal told BBC Sport after Sunday’s final. “I really hoped that one day I would achieve that, and it’s a nice touch to wake up tomorrow [Monday] and see that statistic. “I’m so proud of this week. item.title: MM 10.19: Maryland football fires defensive coordinator Ted Monachino
item.description: Mar 5, 2022; Indianapolis, IN, USA; Atlanta Falcons coach Ted Monachino reacts during the 2022 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Maryland football made a coaching change ahead of its bye week, but not the one fans were expecting. Defensive coordinator and outside linebackers coach Ted Monachino was fired Sunday, ending his time with the program. Terrapins Make Change at Defensive Coordinator Position https://t.co/269LMby1wm — Maryland Football (@TerpsFootball) October 18, 2026 Monachino’s defense has conceded the eighth-most points (233) in the country this season, including nearly 44 per game during its five-game skid. The Terps gave up at least 40 points in three straight games and allowed Rutgers to score 24 second-half points Saturday. “I appreciate Ted’s hard work and dedication to our program during his time in College Park,” head coach Michael Locksley said. “As I evaluate our program, I believe this change is necessary. We wish Ted all the best moving forward.” Maryland, who was tied for the Big Ten lead with 19 interceptions in 2025, has allowed 451.6 yards per game against power conference foes this season. UCLA, Nebraska and then-No. 5 Ohio State each rushed for over 200 yards during their blowout wins over the Terps. Saturday’s 37-30 defeat marked Maryland’s 12th consecutive loss in Big Ten games, the longest active streak in the conference. The Terps haven’t won a home Big Ten contest since Oct. 19, 2024, recording one conference victory in each of their previous seasons. Maryland has yet to secure its first Big Ten win in 2026. Aazaar Abdul-Rahim will serve as defensive coordinator for the remainder of the season, while inside linebackers coach Zac Spavital will assume the role of co-defensive coordinator. In other news Maryland men’s basketball overcame a 15-point halftime deficit to produce a thrilling 90-81 overtime exhibition victory over West Virginia. Dylan Schmidt covered the game. Maryland football allowed 24 unanswered points en route to a 37-30 defeat to Rutgers for its fifth consecutive loss. Jude Wilkenfeld wrote the recap , and Dylan Schmidt gave his takeaways . No. 1 Maryland field hockey notched a pair of 4-0 wins over Michigan State and Ohio State . Roman Brunetti had the story. No. 14 Maryland men’s soccer needed an 85th-minute game-winner to earn a 3-2 victory over Michigan. Rize Simmons had the coverage . Maryland volleyball fell in straight sets to No. 6 Wisconsin and No. 21 Minnesota . Aarna Mishra provided the recaps. Maryland women’s soccer dropped its home finale, 3-1, to Iowa. Noah Ghelli wrote the story. Maryland baseball tied 4-4 against Georgetown in game one before ending the doubleheader with a commanding 9-4 victory. item.title: Chiefs News: Patrick Mahomes matches Tom Brady through 100 career wins
item.description: (Photo by Matthew J. Lee/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs keep winning, and the latest in five consecutive victories to start this season put quarterback Patrick Mahomes in rarefied air. He tied all-time quarterback Tom Brady for fastest to reach 100 career wins. When asked during his post-game press conference, Mahomes joked about Brady’s incredible success. “My honest first reaction is they’ve said this from 97 on. I’m like, ‘When did (QB) Tom (Brady) lose another game?’” Mahomes said to laughter from the press pool. “Because I feel every game I win, I tie him.” Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes Ties Tom Brady’s All-Time Record in Chargers Win | Heavy Sports Mahomes earned the 100th victory of his career on Sunday, October 18 against the visiting Los Angeles Chargers, joining Brady as the youngest QBs to hit that major milestone. “I mean, it’s awesome. Because, I mean, he’s the GOAT, man,” Mahomes said in an on-field, postgame interview with CBS Sports reporter Melanie Collins. “He’s the one that has kinda shown us how to do it in winning the Super Bowls and winning every single week. So it’s always an honor if you’re mentioned in his name. But it seems like every time I win a game, I’m tying him, so I’m gonna keep winning.” The Chiefs are 5-0 — and their offense may be returning to their dynastic heights | NBC News The last time Kansas City started 5-0 was in the 2024 season, when it finished the regular season 11-0 in one-score games and white-knuckled two playoff wins before getting blown out by the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl. But this is an entirely different 5-0, as the Chiefs are now powered by a highly efficient offense and a capable defense. While Kansas City has been a perennial title contender under Mahomes, this year’s team is much more formidable than it was the last few seasons. That flag wiped out an interception by the Chiefs’ Chris Rolland-Wallace. “To me,” Steratore said, “I just didn’t like the foul for roughing the passer.” Steratore noted Gillotte tried to avoid contact and didn’t throw his body at Herbert. But it seems like every time I win a game, I’m tying him, so I’m gonna keep winning.” The Chiefs are 5-0 — and their offense may be returning to their dynastic heights | NBC News The last time Kansas City started 5-0 was in the 2024 season, when it finished the regular season 11-0 in one-score games and white-knuckled two playoff wins before getting blown out by the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl. But this is an entirely different 5-0, as the Chiefs are now powered by a highly efficient offense and a capable defense. While Kansas City has been a perennial title contender under Mahomes, this year’s team is much more formidable than it was the last few seasons. Roughing-the-passer call on the Chiefs upsets Andy Reid, fans and rules analyst | The Kansas City Star Defensive end Ashton Gillotte was flagged for roughing the passer when he ran into Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. That flag wiped out an interception by the Chiefs’ Chris Rolland-Wallace. “To me,” Steratore said, “I just didn’t like the foul for roughing the passer.” Steratore noted Gillotte tried to avoid contact and didn’t throw his body at Herbert. Fortunately for the Chiefs, they ended up getting an interception later in the drive when linebacker Jack Cochrane picked off Herbert. ‘None of that matters’ – Nick Wright gives ‘dumb’ Kansas City Chiefs verdict after comfortable win | HITC “The Chiefs did literally everything you’re supposed to do to lose a dumb game. They missed an extra point, had a special teams turnover, threw a pick in the end zone & got stuffed at the 1. But, luckily, they were playing the Chargers so none of that matters,” the First Things First star wrote on X. Chiefs defensive back ejected for punching Chargers player | KSHB 41 Initially, both Roland-Wallace and Harkey were called for offsetting personal foul penalties on the first play of the final period. But after an expedited league review, referee Alan Eck announced that Roland-Wallace was ejected for “landing a punch,” leading to jeers inside Arrowhead Stadium. Roland-Wallace, a versatile third-year defensive back from USC, had four tackles, including one for a loss, before the ejection. Around the NFL C.J. Gardner-Johnson apologizes after getting ejected for spitting at Brock Bowers | The Athletic “My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed,” Gardner-Johnson posted on his Instagram story. “The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game. “There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard.” Harbaugh mum on McDaniel, says Chargers need ‘to address everything’ | ESPN “I don’t know,” Herbert said on what hasn’t clicked for him in this offense so far. “If I had the answers, then we’d definitely be having a different conversation.” Harbaugh tried his best to explain what he saw from his quarterback Sunday, saying Herbert “didn’t have a lot of chances” and did everything he could possibly do. However, the coach again mentioned that what the Chargers are doing in preparation is not showing up during games. “Just one of the things that’s not translating from meetings, practice to the game,” Harbaugh said. “Our run game, our passing game, our short-yardage game. Being able to move the ball and score points, whether that’s in the red zone or if we have the ball at the 1 or the 40 or the 50. What’s not translating? How do we get it to translate?” Has the Travis Hunter breakout arrived? Jacksonville CB/WR showcases long-term, two-way potential vs. Texans | CBS Sports Hunter is now the first player with a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game since Pro Football Hall of Famer Brian Dawkins did so back in 2022, also against the Texans. Hunter’s performance on Sunday is now just the fourth time a player has produced a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game (including the playoffs) since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Xavier Worthy rises to the occasion for Chiefs’ offense They told me all week: it’s going to be for me,” Worthy said. “I have to step up for the receiving room; guys are down, and I did my one of 11.” “It’s obviously great to be targeted early and often… getting your feel for the game.” It was a slower pace to the finish line in Kansas City’s 22-6 win over Los Angeles on offense, but Worthy still finished as the team’s leader in receptions (7), receiving yards (73) and yards after catch (43). He caught all seven passes thrown his way and moved the chains four times. item.title: Phillies’ Future Infielder Sends Bo Bichette Message After $126 Million Decision
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 31: Bo Bichette #19 of the New York Mets looks on duing the game against the Miami Marlins at Citi Field on July 31, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies are heading into an offseason with important questions about their infield, including whether Trea Turner will remain at shortstop after a difficult defensive season. Turner’s future could become a defining storyline as the Phillies try to keep their championship window open. The club also has potential changes at third base to consider, with Alec Bohm entering free agency and top prospect Aidan Miller pushing toward the major leagues after missing most of 2026 with a back injury. Miller’s potential role next season — which could come at shortstop or third base depending on how things proceed — as well as some high-profile contract negotiations from last offseason, made his recent message about his baseball role model particularly interesting. “Miller, who models his game after former Phillies free-agent target Bo Bichette, is playing third base in the Fall League, a potential precursor to replacing free agent Alec Bohm,” Scott Lauber relayed for The Philadelphia Inquirer . “But (president of baseball operations Dave) Dombrowski also met with Turner this week and issued what amounted to an ultimatum: Improve your defense, or get moved off shortstop.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets Veteran Shortstop Cuts Ties With Team Shortly After Disappointing Season Philadelphia Phillies’ Mimics Bo Bichette With Shortstop, Third Base Opportunities Ahead Dombrowski made it very clear that Miller could factor into the Phillies’ big-league plans as they evaluate their infield for 2027. The prospect’s ability to handle both shortstop and third base gives the club options, although his eventual position will depend on the roster’s needs and his development. “Shortstop Trea Turner could be asked to move to the outfield, although it is unclear if those conversations will take place,” Todd Zolecki wrote for MLB.com . “Miller is playing third base this fall, which is an AFL roster/playing time consideration more than it is a signal of the Phillies’ future plans for him. He could play third and short next year as he pushes for a promotion.” Miller’s return to the field after a lengthy injury absence has added urgency to the discussion. The 22-year-old prospect has an opportunity to make up for lost development time and potentially push for a major-league role next season. Still, the Phillies have not committed to replacing Turner, and Miller’s fall assignment alone does not guarantee a position change. Turner’s future could become a defining storyline as the Phillies try to keep their championship window open. Miller’s potential role next season — which could come at shortstop or third base depending on how things proceed — as well as some high-profile contract negotiations from last offseason, made his recent message about his baseball role model particularly interesting. “Miller, who models his game after former Phillies free-agent target Bo Bichette, is playing third base in the Fall League, a potential precursor to replacing free agent Alec Bohm,” Scott Lauber relayed for The Philadelphia Inquirer . “But (president of baseball operations Dave) Dombrowski also met with Turner this week and issued what amounted to an ultimatum: Improve your defense, or get moved off shortstop.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets Veteran Shortstop Cuts Ties With Team Shortly After Disappointing Season Philadelphia Phillies’ Mimics Bo Bichette With Shortstop, Third Base Opportunities Ahead Dombrowski made it very clear that Miller could factor into the Phillies’ big-league plans as they evaluate their infield for 2027. The prospect’s ability to handle both shortstop and third base gives the club options, although his eventual position will depend on the roster’s needs and his development. “Shortstop Trea Turner could be asked to move to the outfield, although it is unclear if those conversations will take place,” Todd Zolecki wrote for MLB.com . “Miller is playing third base this fall, which is an AFL roster/playing time consideration more than it is a signal of the Phillies’ future plans for him. He could play third and short next year as he pushes for a promotion.” Miller’s return to the field after a lengthy injury absence has added urgency to the discussion. The 22-year-old prospect has an opportunity to make up for lost development time and potentially push for a major-league role next season. Still, the Phillies have not committed to replacing Turner, and Miller’s fall assignment alone does not guarantee a position change. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers Castoff Catcher Abruptly Ends Career Immediately After Season Ends Philadelphia Phillies Seek Infield Changes After Bo Bichette’s $126 Million Contract Move The Bichette comparison also recalls a significant missed opportunity for Philadelphia last winter. The former Toronto Blue Jays shortstop signed a short-term contract with the New York Mets after declining the Phillies’ pursuit. “A year ago, the Phillies reportedly offered Bichette close to $200 million over eight seasons, but he turned it down knowing a three-year, $126 million contract could set him up to make significantly more than $200 million over that same eight-year period,” Anthony DiComo noted for MLB.com . Bichette’s decision left the Phillies without the star infield addition it had targeted, while his move to third base in New York underscored the positional flexibility that Miller seeks to emulate. Now, Miller represents a potential in-house solution. If Turner remains at shortstop, Miller could still compete for time at third base, particularly if Bohm departs. If Turner moves elsewhere, Miller’s defensive experience at shortstop could become more important. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Manager Stephen Vogt of the Cleveland Guardians signals for a pitching change during the fourth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the American League Championship Series at Progressive Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The World Series matchup isn’t set in stone just yet, but Tampa Bay took a major step towards being the one that will face Milwaukee in the Fall Classic. They took two out of three in Cleveland to return home with a 3-2 series lead heading into a big Game 6 tonight, where they’ll start Freddy Peralta who has been dealing this postseason while the Guardians will scramble to piece their way through a bullpen game after having to get 21 outs from their relievers yesterday. Thanks to the postponed Game 4 eating up the travel day, even if they do win tonight they’ll also be forced to play the potential do-or-die Game 7 on four straight days without a night off — it’s not looking pretty for Cleveland, to say the least. We’ve got a full slate for you ahead of this critical Game 6 later tonight, starting with Jake’s recap of Game 5’s action in the Roundup. Michael hands out a stellar grade to David Bednar to kick off our annual Report Card series, and Kevin recalls Sandy Alomar Sr. and his days with the Yankees on his birthday. Then in the afternoon Jonathan goes over the Yankees’ longest home runs of the season and Estevao reflects on the gap between Giancarlo Stanton and 500 career home runs before I return to open up the mailbag for more of your questions. Today’s Playoff Matchup: American League Championship Series Game 6 (Rays lead series, 3-2) Cleveland Guardians vs. Tampa Bay Rays Time: 8:00 p.m. EST TV: TBS/HBO Max/truTV Venue: Tropicana Field, St. Petersburg, FL Questions/Prompts: 1. With their bullpen depleted ahead of a bullpen game, does Cleveland need a miracle to extend the ALCS or will we see a competitive game? 2. Are you ready for the Knicks’ season opener and banner presentation tomorrow night?

item.title: C.J. Stroud’s fourth-quarter comeback kept the Texans alive against Jacksonville
item.description: C.J. Stroud’s fourth-quarter comeback kept the Texans alive against Jacksonville originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Texans left London with a win that looked unlikely late in the game. Ka’imi Fairbairn’s 49-yard field goal as time expired completed a 34-31 comeback against the Jacksonville Jaguars and gave Houston one of the most dramatic finishes of Week 6. C.J. Stroud was central to the rally. He passed for 312 yards and three touchdowns, repeatedly giving Houston a chance to stay within reach after Jacksonville threatened to take control. The result is especially important because the Texans entered the game with a 1-4 record. A loss would have made the path back into the AFC South race more difficult. Instead, Houston moved to 2-4 and handed Jacksonville its second defeat. A wild finish in London The game was not decided until the final possession. Houston’s offense put the Texans in position for Fairbairn, who converted the 49-yard attempt to secure the victory. The kick capped a game in which both teams had opportunities to seize control. WHAT A THROW FROM CJ STROUD. HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/Z8LUxZceAl — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Jacksonville’s offense had enough success to put up 31 points, but the Jaguars could not close the door. Stroud’s three touchdown passes kept Houston in the game, and the Texans found the final points they needed when the pressure was highest. A road win in an international game can also complicate preparation and routine. Houston had to manage the travel and the unusual setting while facing a divisional opponent that came in with a far stronger record. MORE : Browns’ defense flips the script as Cleveland stuns Ravens The Texans have something to build on One win does not fix Houston’s uneven start, but a last-second victory against a 4-1 team gives the Texans a meaningful result to carry into next week. Stroud’s production is an encouraging sign, particularly after the team needed a high-pressure finish. For Jacksonville, the loss will sting because the Jaguars had a chance to strengthen their grip on the division. Instead, the final kick flipped the story. The Texans now have a result that can change the mood around their season. They still have work to do, but Sunday’s finish showed they can respond when a game reaches its most demanding moment. More NFL news: Joey Porter Jr. news considered ‘good’ after Steelers trade JJ McCarthy gets major starting job prediction despite New York’s 3-1 start Vikings get positive Justin Jefferson update after making wise decision against Dolphins

item.title: Markus Krösche set to become AC Milan’s new Head of Football
item.description: Markus Krösche set to become AC Milan’s new Head of Football As reported by Kicker , Markus Krösche is set to become AC Milan’s new Head of Football. On Sunday evening, the bombshell spread like wildfire around German football – Markus Krösche is to leave his role as Eintracht Frankfurt Sporting Director with immediate effect. The 46-year-old asked if he could be released from his duties, stating that he “needed a change.” The change in question appears to be a move to Serie A and AC Milan as their new Head of Football. Krösche’s departure had been rumoured last summer, but nothing materialised. However, the iron is now hot, and an official agreement with Milan is expected to be announced this week. Milan already had Krösche in their sights last summer, offering him a four-year deal totalling up to €40m. As stated in Gazzetta dello Sport , these discussions never went away; instead, both parties were just trying to come to an agreement when it came to the job, its duties, and, of course, finances. Eintracht Frankfurt to Receive Transfer Fee for Markus Krösche The one plus side in all of this for Frankfurt is that they will receive a transfer fee should Krösche move to Milan. The 46-year-old is under contract until 2028 and would therefore need to be bought out of his current deal. How much Milan are willing to spend is not yet known. GGFN | Jamie Allen
