item.title: Clemson Dominates Charleston Southern Despite Offensive Ineptitude
item.description: CLEMSON, SC - OCTOBER 17: Clemson Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney congratulates his offense after they scored a touchdown during a college football game between the Charleston Southern Buccaneers and the Clemson Tigers on October 17, 2026 at Clemson Memorial Stadium in Clemson, S.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Clemson hosted Charleston Southern in a game that was always a question about how much they would win by, not if they would ever win. Thankfully Clemson’s defense showed up for all four quarters while the offensive continued to be here in name only. Thankfully it was enough for a 37-0 victory. We always caution about taking away too many positives from cupcake games. But the defense absolutely get credit. A shutout with only 76 yards of offense allowed is always a great day. Yes, Charleston Southern had a great set of scripted plays on the first drive and a few other opportunities lost due to drops and other miscues, but defense did exactly what they needed to. The offense, well it really is hard to say much beyond “They stink”. Sure we can all talk about a season high in scoring, but the truth is the Tigers scored 30 points against an FCS team. And for our starters that’s only 27 points. Against an FCS team. That’s not great. Sure put on a nice face in public, but even factoring in Dabo’s desire to not embarrass teams this is a bad performance. This offense had a single explosive play with the starters in, a 32-yard pass to Bentancur. There were only 2 other passes that exceeded 10 yards, going for 11 and 10 yards respectively. This is not an explosive offense. Much like the last 5 years this is an occasionally efficient offense. That doesn’t win games against top teams. It barely wins you games against the middle of the pack. Sustaining a drive that consists of solely 3-5 yard plays just isn’t going to work. Top line stats look fine. 400 yards of offense, close to 50% on third downs, and nearly 30 first downs. Everyone loves those numbers, but it should mean more than 37 points. Hey at least special teams got some points, more efficient than our offense too. Buckly up for Virginia Tech, it could get ugly again.

item.title: This is the beginning of the end for this iteration of the Colts
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Head coach Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts looks on during the fourth quarter against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chris Ballard era is over. Shane Steichen at the helm is no more. Daniel Jones as the quarterback for the Indianapolis Colts is on incredibly thin ice. Losing to the Tennessee Titans sure feels like the straw that will break the camel’s back. For a season in which the motto is “Find a Way”, the only thing this organization needs to find a way to do is to push the reset button. It’s been six weeks, so saying it’s all over is tough. A lot can change with two-thirds of the season left. The biggest issue is the here and now. After falling to the winless Titans at home, the Colts find themselves at 2-4. That is the now. The immediate future is bleak as well. Not to say that the Colts can’t win but the undefeated Vikings and the Jaguars, both on the road, lie ahead. Ask yourself if you see those games going well. Time is up. The beginning part of this season was do or die. Finding a way didn’t mean find a way to lose to the worst team in football. Props to the Colts for finding creative ways to lose, but that isn’t what Carlie Irsay-Gordon had in mind. Ballard’s seat is so hot that it should have already melted. Steichen hasn’t shown enough to make it out of this. The failures are evident and felt by the players too. This is rock bottom and change is needed. Patience is a virtue, but it isn’t a requirement in the NFL. The Irsays have shown enough over the years to this staff and personnel. Daniel Jones doesn’t have the juice. Shane Steichen has shown an inability to win. Chris Ballard has failed to put a good product on the field 90% of the time. We knew this was coming. Sunday’s disaster was the gust of wind that will topple this house of cards.

item.title: NBA Restricts Sportsbook Bets — Will Kalshi and Polymarket Follow?
item.description: The NBA’s new sportsbook restrictions highlight questions over whether prediction exchanges will adopt equivalent betting limits. Key Takeaways The NBA is restricting several betting markets offered by its sportsbook partners. Its sportsbook agreements do not give it equivalent control over Kalshi and Polymarket. The changes raise questions about the consistency of integrity protections across competing platforms. The NBA is tightening control over bets that could reward manipulated performances, but its authority does not extend to every platform where fans trade on basketball outcomes. As prediction exchanges fall outside the NBA’s agreements, this raises the question of whether they will adopt the same limits as concern over insider trading grows. Which Bets Is the NBA Restricting? According to InGame, which cites a league letter obtained by ESPN, the restrictions include: Parlays combining multiple statistical unders for the same player. Wagers on the winner of the opening tip. Certain negative outcomes involving individual plays, including missed shots. Unders on players expected to play fewer than 12 minutes. An under wins when a player finishes below a specified statistical threshold. Combining several unders can allow a bettor to profit across multiple categories if that player makes an unexpectedly early exit. DraftKings said the changes partly formalize limits it already applies. “The NBA’s guidance formalizes many of the market restrictions already reflected in DraftKings Sportsbook’s practices,” a spokesperson told InGame. Why Player Unders Have Become an Integrity Concern The restrictions address a vulnerability first exposed by the Jontay Porter scandal; advance knowledge of limited playing time can affect several wagers simultaneously. The NBA banned Porter in April 2024 after finding that he had wagered on NBA games and even limited his participation for betting-related reasons. For example, an early departure off the court can reduce a player’s opportunities to score and assist. A bettor who therefore knows about a planned departure beforehand could hold an advantage across those two markets. What Are Kalshi and Polymarket Offering? Public pages reviewed by CCN on Oct. 19 show that both exchanges offer NBA trading. Kalshi’s basketball hub lists individual matchups alongside spread and total markets. Polymarket US also lists upcoming NBA games, while its separate international platform carries markets including the 2027 championship. As CCN previously explained , sports prediction contracts have become a focal point of the dispute between federal derivatives regulation and state gambling oversight. An exchange contract and a sportsbook wager can expose users to the same sporting outcome, yet operate under different regulatory structures. A future agreement with a prediction exchange could give the league greater contractual influence over that operator’s products. Legal Sports Report reported that the NBA had not announced such a
item.content:encoded: The NBA’s new sportsbook restrictions highlight questions over whether prediction exchanges will adopt equivalent betting limits. Key Takeaways The NBA is restricting several betting markets offered by its sportsbook partners. Its sportsbook agreements do not give it equivalent control over Kalshi and Polymarket. The changes raise questions about the consistency of integrity protections across competing platforms. The NBA is tightening control over bets that could reward manipulated performances, but its authority does not extend to every platform where fans trade on basketball outcomes. As prediction exchanges fall outside the NBA’s agreements, this raises the question of whether they will adopt the same limits as concern over insider trading grows. Which Bets Is the NBA Restricting? According to InGame, which cites a league letter obtained by ESPN, the restrictions include: Parlays combining multiple statistical unders for the same player. Wagers on the winner of the opening tip. Certain negative outcomes involving individual plays, including missed shots. Unders on players expected to play fewer than 12 minutes. An under wins when a player finishes below a specified statistical threshold. Combining several unders can allow a bettor to profit across multiple categories if that player makes an unexpectedly early exit. DraftKings said the changes partly formalize limits it already applies. “The NBA’s guidance formalizes many of the market restrictions already reflected in DraftKings Sportsbook’s practices,” a spokesperson told InGame. Why Player Unders Have Become an Integrity Concern The restrictions address a vulnerability first exposed by the Jontay Porter scandal; advance knowledge of limited playing time can affect several wagers simultaneously. The NBA banned Porter in April 2024 after finding that he had wagered on NBA games and even limited his participation for betting-related reasons. For example, an early departure off the court can reduce a player’s opportunities to score and assist. A bettor who therefore knows about a planned departure beforehand could hold an advantage across those two markets. What Are Kalshi and Polymarket Offering? Public pages reviewed by CCN on Oct. 19 show that both exchanges offer NBA trading. Kalshi’s basketball hub lists individual matchups alongside spread and total markets. Polymarket US also lists upcoming NBA games, while its separate international platform carries markets including the 2027 championship. As CCN previously explained , sports prediction contracts have become a focal point of the dispute between federal derivatives regulation and state gambling oversight. An exchange contract and a sportsbook wager can expose users to the same sporting outcome, yet operate under different regulatory structures. A future agreement with a prediction exchange could give the league greater contractual influence over that operator’s products. Legal Sports Report reported that the NBA had not announced such a partnership when the restrictions emerged. Prediction Markets Face Growing Scrutiny The NBA’s restrictions arrive amid broader questions about whether prediction markets adequately protect users against insider trading and manipulation. In May, House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer launched an investigation into Kalshi and Polymarket, requesting information about identity checks and how the platforms detect suspicious trading. “As online prediction platforms grow and become more mainstream, some bad actors have exploited the platforms to make thousands of dollars by placing bets based on nonpublic information,” said Chairman Comer. “Americans deserve to know that these platforms are taking steps to prevent insider trading,” he added. Concerns have already led to concrete disciplinary action. In February, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued an advisory following two Kalshi cases involving misuse of nonpublic information and fraud. “In May 2025, social media posts contained videos that appeared to show a political candidate trading on his own candidacy on Kalshi,” the CFTC wrote in its report. Meanwhile, in August and September 2025, “an individual traded a prediction market related to a YouTube channel while having an employment relationship… with the subject of the contract.” Critics have also challenged whether sports contracts allow operators to bypass protections required of state-licensed gambling businesses. As CCN previously reported , state regulators and tribal groups have contested the industry’s reliance on federal derivatives oversight, arguing that sports contracts amount to gambling subject to additional restrictions. The post NBA Restricts Sportsbook Bets — Will Kalshi and Polymarket Follow? appeared first on ccn.com .

item.title: Who plays on 'Monday Night Football' tonight? Time, TV channel, schedule, live stream for NFL Week 6 game
item.description: Who plays on 'Monday Night Football' tonight? Time, TV channel, schedule, live stream for NFL Week 6 game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The story for the 49ers entering the season was injuries, right down to head coach Kyle Shanahan. The story since the start of the season has been success. While injuries certainly have been a factor for the 'Niners, from Nick Bosa to De'Zhaun Stribling and Deebo Samuel, Shanahan's group has found a way to thrive in spite of them. After the 49ers won in Seattle in Week 5, the NFC West could just be a race for second behind San Francisco. On the other side of the country, the Commanders have managed just one win in five games. That doesn't mean they have four losses, though. Washington settled for a tie in Week 5, after a disastrous final sequence that largely remains unexplained. Coach Dan Quinn said after the game that it felt like a loss, and it's hard to argue with that. Going on the road and handing the 49ers their first loss would unquestionably be a win, though. The upset-minded Commanders are hoping to channel last weekend's frustration and leave the west coast feeling like they can compete in a wide-open NFC East race. With that, here's what you need to know to watch "Monday Night Football" in Week 6. Who plays on Monday Night Football tonight? Matchup: Commanders vs. 49ers Location: Levi's Stadium, Santa Clara, CA "Monday Night Football" is headed to the Bay Area in Week 6, with the undefeated 49ers hosting the Commanders. What time is the NFL game on tonight? Date: Monday, Oct. 19 Time: 8:15 p.m. ET | 5:15 p.m. PT Commanders vs. 49ers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET (5:15 p.m. local time) from Levi's Stadium on Monday night. What channel is Monday Night Football on tonight? TV channel: ESPN Live stream: DIRECTV | ESPN | Fubo "Monday Night Football" will be simulcast live on ESPN, with Joe Buck (play-by-play) in the booth alongside Troy Aikman (analyst) from SoFi Stadium. item.title: Why do Man City fans have inflatable bananas? Explaining retro fan craze in defiance of Premier League guilty verdict
item.description: Why do Man City fans have inflatable bananas? Explaining retro fan craze in defiance of Premier League guilty verdict originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . So much of the build-up to the October 11 Premier League showdown between Liverpool and Manchester City was dominated by discussions about the atmosphere. The Anfield crowd was anticipated to bring an extreme state of vitriolic hostility and fury to the occasion, as City stepped out for the first time since the Premier League found them guilty of all charges related to serious financial breaches of competition rules between 2009/10 and 2017/18. Just after the period that was examined by an independent commission and resulted in a shockingly damning verdict – where City were found to have concocted "sham" sponsorship agreements with companies from Abu Dhabi and put forward witnesses believed to have lied – Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool went blow-for-blow with Pep Guardiola's City in thrilling title races in 2018/19 and 2021/22. Twice Liverpool racked up in excess of 90 points; twice they lost the league by a point. Andoni Iraola and Enzo Maresca led the two sides, and few of the main characters from those incredible battles remained. Enmity on the Kop, understandably, did. MORE: Jurgen Klopp lands on deeper Pep Guardiola truth amid 115 charges "Absolutely, [the City players] can face the pressure," a relaxed Enzo Maresca said at his pre-match press conference. "We have players who have experience of similar situations. Enzo Fernandez played in Argentina. In Argentina, almost every game is like you go to Anfield." The response from City's travelling supporters, viewed by millions of television viewers across the world as they raucously celebrated a 3-0 win , invited puzzlement. Tucked away in the left-hand corner of the Anfield Road End, the Mancunian contingent brandished dozens upon dozens of large inflatable bananas. It was the same story at City's first Premier League home game after the verdict — a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town — as thousands of inflatable bananas dotted a capacity 60,000 attendance at the Etihad Stadium. item.content:encoded: Why do Man City fans have inflatable bananas? Explaining retro fan craze in defiance of Premier League guilty verdict originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . So much of the build-up to the October 11 Premier League showdown between Liverpool and Manchester City was dominated by discussions about the atmosphere. The Anfield crowd was anticipated to bring an extreme state of vitriolic hostility and fury to the occasion, as City stepped out for the first time since the Premier League found them guilty of all charges related to serious financial breaches of competition rules between 2009/10 and 2017/18. Just after the period that was examined by an independent commission and resulted in a shockingly damning verdict – where City were found to have concocted "sham" sponsorship agreements with companies from Abu Dhabi and put forward witnesses believed to have lied – Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool went blow-for-blow with Pep Guardiola's City in thrilling title races in 2018/19 and 2021/22. Twice Liverpool racked up in excess of 90 points; twice they lost the league by a point. Andoni Iraola and Enzo Maresca led the two sides, and few of the main characters from those incredible battles remained. Enmity on the Kop, understandably, did. MORE: Jurgen Klopp lands on deeper Pep Guardiola truth amid 115 charges "Absolutely, [the City players] can face the pressure," a relaxed Enzo Maresca said at his pre-match press conference. "We have players who have experience of similar situations. Enzo Fernandez played in Argentina. In Argentina, almost every game is like you go to Anfield." The response from City's travelling supporters, viewed by millions of television viewers across the world as they raucously celebrated a 3-0 win , invited puzzlement. Tucked away in the left-hand corner of the Anfield Road End, the Mancunian contingent brandished dozens upon dozens of large inflatable bananas. It was the same story at City's first Premier League home game after the verdict — a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town — as thousands of inflatable bananas dotted a capacity 60,000 attendance at the Etihad Stadium. Phil Foden arrived for his post-match interview with an inflatable banana 🍌 https://t.co/15brfnndUb — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) October 17, 2026 Why do Man City fans have inflatable bananas? The origin story of Manchester City's near 40-year association with inflatable bananas goes back to the 1987/88 season, the club's first back in Division Two after being relegated from Division One the previous year. Like a lot of the best stories, it features some palpably rubbish wordplay. "It started because of [former City forward] Imre Varadi," said Dante Friend of 1894 , the City fan group who have distributed upwards of 1,000 inflatable bananas among supporters traveling to Anfield. "It was just one guy at the game who referred to him as "Imre Banana". A guy called Frank Newton took an inflatable banana to the next game, and then everyone started doing it." There were all sorts of other inflatables, from paddling pools to fried eggs and Frankenstein's monster, but it was the bananas that endured. Sometimes in this job, you find yourself writing the strangest sentences imaginable. Varadi enjoyed a nomadic career in English football, representing City, Everton , Sheffield Wednesday and Leeds among many others. He scored 31 times in 81 appearances for City across all competitions, a very solid return at a time when the club was not at its best on the field. His wider legacy has nothing to do with any of those goals, and it's one he continues to embrace. "The bananas are taking over Anfield," Varadi posted on X (account handle: @imre_banana ) on the morning of the Liverpool match. "City fans are ready to party at Liverpool." 🍌🍌 The bananas are taking over Anfield! ⚽ Great to see our inflatable bananas getting a mention on Sky Sports this morning and making the back page of the Daily Star! 📰 City fans are ready to party at Liverpool! 💙🍌 #MCFC — Imre Varadi (@imre_banana) October 11, 2026 Manchester also knew how to throw a party during the mid-to-late 1980s, as the acid house music scene that in turn spawned the 'Madchester' craze thrived. The famous Hacienda nightclub was the high church of the movement – a temple of optimism and love via chemical refreshment, that stood at odds with the often desolate state of hooligan-addled English football as Margaret Thatcher's conservative government oversaw a period of post-industrial decline in many of the country's biggest cities. "The reason some people were doing it as a joke was because they were going out clubbing on a Friday night to places like the Hacienda and the Brickhouse and were absolutely off their heads on ecstasy, then falling into the match the next afternoon," Friend recalled. "They weren't interested in fighting. Most of the fans were having a laugh. We were s—, we were in Division Two. I think, every now and then, when it's fan-led and not club-led, [bringing back the bananas] can be really good. It'll be a laugh." Getty Images And that's the spirit being tapped into as Manchester City, to many, embark on a new chapter as pariahs of English football. The spirit of a club founded in 1894 that won its first trophy in 1904 and has seen all sorts of majestically brilliant, perplexingly bad and mind-numbingly average iterations throughout this long history. Their trajectory was changed beyond all recognition by Sheikh Mansour's 2008 takeover. Pending an appeal, the wrongdoing of the Abu Dhabi royal's trusted executives will change that path once again. But nothing is permanent. Manchester City were here before their current ownership, and it would be a travesty for generation upon generation of fans if they weren't after them. MORE: Man City owners' fraud punishes players and fans more than Premier League ever can When City struggled in the 1980s and again, even more severely in the 1990s, inflatable bananas were there to celebrate every promotion back to the big time. They've featured in every pitch invasion after every Premier League success at the Etihad Stadium. Whatever those titles mean now, they promoted grown adults to wave ridiculous, oversized novelty fruit above their heads. Because sport is brilliant like that. The reborn banana craze is a show of defiance from City fans, who before the days of billion-dollar spending counted gallows humour and sarcasm as their most potent weapons. They're not scared to go back there if they have to. Don't threaten them with a good time. "The message is obviously defiance," Friend added. "We don't give a f— who the owners are, we are the club. The fans are the club."

item.title: ‘League in Shambles,’ ‘Huge Signing’ – Jalen Williams, NBA Fans React to Thunder’s ‘Ridiculous’ $139 Million Decision on Cason Wallace
item.description: Cason Wallace and the OKC Thunder have agreed to a five-year, $139 million contract extension. Here's what the NBA world has to say. Right before the 2026-27 NBA season officially tips off, the Oklahoma City Thunder and Cason Wallace agreed to a five-year, $139 million contract extension. A massive deal, the rookie-scale contract will ensure Wallace remains with the team until the 2031-32 season. Confirmed by agents Jeff Schwartz, Max Lipsett, and Marcus Monk of Excel Sports Management, the new contract generated a lot of buzz, especially as many fans considered the real implications of such a commitment from the Thunder and Wallace. Jalen Williams, NBA Fans Weigh In on Thunder-Cason Wallace Deal A first-round pick in 2023, Wallace has steadily made his way up the NBA ladder over the past few seasons. The Thunder, looking to reclaim success, are ensuring every player on their roster is accounted for. Of course, signing Wallace in 2026 was an important move, especially as they looked to avoid lucrative offers if he became a restricted free agent next year. “Oklahoma City Thunder All-Defensive guard Cason Wallace has agreed to a five-year, $139 million rookie-scale contract extension, agents Jeff Schwartz, Max Lipsett and Marcus Monk of Excel Sports Management tell ESPN,” Shams Charania reported on Sunday night. Fans, however, had varying opinions on the five-year deal. Journalist Rylan Stiles, who covers OKC, was quick to react as he wrote : “Huge signing for Oklahoma City.” While many agreed with Stiles, some fans believed the signing was a big mistake, with one claiming it reflected on the NBA itself. This includes teams signing young players to large contracts they don’t need to lock down just yet. “… 😂 28 million is ridiculous,” the user wrote . “League in shambles 😭😭😭,” another hoops fan said . Of course, Wallace’s teammate Jalen Williams was happy and expressed his reaction with a three-word message. “Right on time,” Williams posted on Instagram. Some users agreed with both sides, pointing out that while Wallace is a good player, a contract this big is an overpay. “Cason Wallace is a good player. This is an overpay. 2 things can be true,” the fan stated on X. ESPN insider Bobby Marks explained the deal and Thunder’s position further as he wrote : “And yes, OKC is a projected second apron team (right now they are $26M over) and face a tax bill that could exceed $200M. But as the apron rules teach us, the restrictions apply to adding to your roster in free agency and trades, not with retaining your own players.” “Great deal for Wallace and the Thunder,” OKC beat writer Brandon Rahbar added . This also holds true after impressive production last season. Wallace averaged 8.6 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game while shooting 43.2% from the field and 35.1% from the three-point range. He also earned an All-Defensive Second Team honor with 150 steals. DON’T MISS: ‘It Doesn’t Count’ — Klay Thompson Gets Defiant As Nightmarish Preseason Fuels Fears of Heat Sharpshooter’s Further Decline “I think the greatest sign of respect we could have shown Cason is moving Lu in that trade,” Sam Presti explained . “We potentially could have looked at a series of other options, but it’s a bit of a gesture to him to say, ‘We think you can have a great role on this team. We believe in you as a player. And we’re hopeful that (contract extension talks) can work out.’” The Thunder have also generally relied on depth, and the 22-year-old’s presence will only add to their arsenal as they open their 2026-27 season against the San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday, October 20. item.title: Ballon d’Or odds: Kane favourite ahead of Yamal, Rodri and Mbappe
item.description: The Ballon d’Or may be heading to Germany, with Harry Kane back as the favourite to lift the trophy on betting sites . After scoring 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country, including six goals for England at the World Cup, Kane has been reinstalled as the favourite to clinch world football’s top individual honour. The race previously shifted in favour of Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, with the teenager going odds-on with the bookies after he played his part in Spain becoming the world champions for only the second time. But ahead of the glittering ceremony on October 26, the England skipper could be about to add even more honours to his already impressive CV. 2026 Ballon d’Or odds Were Kane to win the Ballon d’Or, he’d be only the fifth Englishman to clinch the prize and the first since Michael Owen in 2001. He was installed as the early frontrunner by football betting sites after a storming 2025/26 campaign. Kane’s form since joining the German giants has been incredible, with 152 goals in 154 appearances as he helped his side to two Bundesliga titles, the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup and the German Cup. On a personal level, he has been the Bundesliga’s top scorer for each of his three seasons in Germany, including last season when he finished with 36 goals in 31 league appearances. His form for England has been equally impressive this year too, with the ex-Tottenham forward taking his tally to 91 goals and counting for the national side, playing a starring role in their run to the World Cup semi-finals. Ballon d’Or betting: Yamal is still a major contender Despite Kane’s goalscoring exploits, the Ballon d’Or betting market recently shifted in favour of Yamal, who was as short as 1/2 on some betting apps before Kane’s latest surge. The 19-year-old has enjoyed another remarkable season, helping Barcelona win La Liga before going to North America, where he was a part of the Spain side that defeated Argentina in the World Cup final. The teenager finished as runner-up to Ousmane Dembele in last year's Ballon d’Or, and in addition to the World Cup win, he scored 25 goals for club and country last term, but he only found the net once at the World Cup. His Spain teammate Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or in 2024 after helping Manchester City to the Premier League title and La Roja to the 2024 European Championships, was also as high as the fifth favourite behind Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi, but he’s now drifted out to 100/1. He started every single game for Spain at the World Cup and picked up the Golden Ball award, but he has now slipped behind the likes of Bukayo Saka, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Cristiano Ronaldo and Dominik Szoboszlai in the betting. Ballon d’Or 2026 odds: Golden Boot enough for Mbappe? Kylian Mbappe also tasted disappointment at the World Cup as France finished fourth, but he won the Golden Boot for the second tournament in a row after scoring 10 and assisting a further four goals. item.title: England manager Wiegman signs contract extension
item.description: Sarina Wiegman has been in charge of England for more than five years [Getty Images] England manager Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension with the Lionesses. The 56-year-old's previous deal was due to expire after next summer's World Cup, but her new contract will run until the end of Euro 2029. Dutchwoman Wiegman guided England to their second straight European Championship title with victory over Spain in the Euro 2025 final. The victory meant the Lionesses became the first England team - women's or men's - to win a major trophy on foreign soil. "I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football," said Wiegman. "Working for a world-class organisation like The FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day." England thrashed Greece 8-1 on aggregate last week to qualify for round two of the World Cup play-offs, where they will face Ukraine. Should the Lionesses win that two-legged tie, they will qualify for next summer's World Cup in Brazil. "My main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come," Wiegman added. "We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year." Wiegman replaced Phil Neville as England manager in September 2021, guiding the Lionesses to their first piece of major silverware at Euro 2022 when they beat Germany 2-1 in the final at Wembley. England then reached the World Cup final in Australia in 2023, only to lose 1-0 to Spain. By reaching the 2025 Euros final, Wiegman became the first women's or men's manager to reach five consecutive major international finals after leading the Netherlands to the Euro 2017 title and runners-up at the 2019 World Cup. England's Euro 2025 victory meant Wiegman became just the second manager after Germany's Christina Theune to win three successive European Championships. FA chief Mark Bullingham described Wiegman as an "incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments". "While we will all remember the trophies and thrilling moments she has given us, I know she is only looking forward," Bullingham added. "There is no one better to lead the Lionesses into the next two tournaments. "Sarina's impact on English football has been immense, and she continues to inspire so many throughout the game. We have so much more to do in the women's game and she will be instrumental in helping us to achieve that." Does Scott's Disney+ exit unmask wider issue in coverage of women's game? Contract a welcome surprise - analysis The FA and England fans alike will be delighted that the 'Wiegman era' is set to continue beyond the 2027 World Cup. Having led the Lionesses to back-to-back European titles and the 2023 World Cup final, many expected Wiegman to leave after next summer's tournament in Bra
item.content:encoded: Sarina Wiegman has been in charge of England for more than five years [Getty Images] England manager Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension with the Lionesses. The 56-year-old's previous deal was due to expire after next summer's World Cup, but her new contract will run until the end of Euro 2029. Dutchwoman Wiegman guided England to their second straight European Championship title with victory over Spain in the Euro 2025 final. The victory meant the Lionesses became the first England team - women's or men's - to win a major trophy on foreign soil. "I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football," said Wiegman. "Working for a world-class organisation like The FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day." England thrashed Greece 8-1 on aggregate last week to qualify for round two of the World Cup play-offs, where they will face Ukraine. Should the Lionesses win that two-legged tie, they will qualify for next summer's World Cup in Brazil. "My main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come," Wiegman added. "We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year." Wiegman replaced Phil Neville as England manager in September 2021, guiding the Lionesses to their first piece of major silverware at Euro 2022 when they beat Germany 2-1 in the final at Wembley. England then reached the World Cup final in Australia in 2023, only to lose 1-0 to Spain. By reaching the 2025 Euros final, Wiegman became the first women's or men's manager to reach five consecutive major international finals after leading the Netherlands to the Euro 2017 title and runners-up at the 2019 World Cup. England's Euro 2025 victory meant Wiegman became just the second manager after Germany's Christina Theune to win three successive European Championships. FA chief Mark Bullingham described Wiegman as an "incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments". "While we will all remember the trophies and thrilling moments she has given us, I know she is only looking forward," Bullingham added. "There is no one better to lead the Lionesses into the next two tournaments. "Sarina's impact on English football has been immense, and she continues to inspire so many throughout the game. We have so much more to do in the women's game and she will be instrumental in helping us to achieve that." Does Scott's Disney+ exit unmask wider issue in coverage of women's game? Contract a welcome surprise - analysis The FA and England fans alike will be delighted that the 'Wiegman era' is set to continue beyond the 2027 World Cup. Having led the Lionesses to back-to-back European titles and the 2023 World Cup final, many expected Wiegman to leave after next summer's tournament in Brazil in search of a new challenge. Instead, her commitment to stay until 2029 underlines the strength of her relationship with the FA and her team. While today's announcement may have surprised some, the timing now allows Wiegman and the players to focus fully on World Cup qualification, without the distraction of a looming succession plan. Widely regarded as one of the game's greatest-ever coaches, Wiegman has already achieved what few can match. But even after three consecutive Euros, this contract extension proves she still has an appetite for more as she chases an elusive World Cup title. Head here to get involved

item.title: ‘Dak Prescott Has To Play Better’ — Robert Griffin III Argues Cowboys QB Looked Like a ‘Human Punching Bag’ In Primetime Loss to Packers
item.description: ‘Dak Prescott Looked Like a Human Punching Bag’ — Robert Griffin III, Ex-NFL Safety Raise Red Flags After Cowboys’ Embarrassing Primetime Loss to Packers Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys suffered a 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football, extending their losing streak to two games and dropping the team to 2-4. The ugly run has been a major blow for the Cowboys, who entered the season with playoff aspirations. Their disappointing performance against Green Bay also drew reactions from several former NFL stars, including Robert Griffin III. Dak Prescott and Cowboys Face Growing Concerns as Robert Griffin III Highlights Major Issues Prescott faced constant pressure from the Packers’ defense on Sunday, throwing two interceptions in the first half. He completed 63% of his passes for 258 yards and one touchdown, along with two interceptions. Prescott currently ranks No. 15 in PFN’s QB Impact Metric with a 76.7 grade. Following Dallas’ loss, Griffin shared three major takeaways from the game, with his first focusing on Prescott and the Cowboys’ offensive line. “Dak Prescott has to play better, and the offensive line has to play better so he isn’t a human punching bag in the pocket,” Griffin wrote . “Because the defense’s reputation cannot keep giving the offense a free pass. Dallas was using star WRs CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens like supporting actors in the first half. “At halftime, Lamb had two catches for 22 yards on six targets, and Pickens had one catch for 16 yards on one target. Three catches for 38 yards isn’t winning football. They need more quality targets and schemes that generate easy completions for them and Dak Prescott.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Former NFL safety Justin Simmons also weighed in on Dallas’ offensive struggles, expressing confidence in the team’s offensive line and its talented receiving duo. Simmons said that, outside the Cincinnati Bengals’ pairing of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, Lamb and Pickens could arguably form the best wide receiver duo in the league. However, Simmons questioned why the Cowboys were not doing more to get the ball into their hands. DIVE IN: PFN’s Free NFL HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More “I’m more concerned about creativity. I’m more concerned about the play calling itself,” Simmons said. “As great as Dak is, every quarterback needs to get into a rhythm to start the football game, and we’re not seeing that.. I feel like we’re asking Dak to step onto the football field and take all the burden of being one of the best quarterbacks in the league and to decipher every single play. “Are they doing this? Are they doing that? And even for Dak Prescott, that could be too much. So you got to be able to run the ball, and you got to be able to set him up with easy, quick throws to these star receivers, so that they can get running.” Dallas’ defensive struggles were equally concerning in the first half, as the Cowboys had virtually no answer for Green Bay on third down, allowing the Packers to convert 9 of 10 attempts through the opening two quarters. Dallas limited Green Bay to just two conversions on eight third-down attempts in the second half while allowing only six points after the break. The Cowboys will now turn their attention to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26, on Monday Night Football. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Sarina Wiegman signs two-year contract extension as England head coach
item.description: FILE PHOTO - England's coach Sarina Wiegman speaks during a press conference for the England women's national soccer team at Wembley Stadium, ahead of Sunday's UEFA Women's EURO 2022 final match against Germany. (is associated with: «Sarina Wiegman signs two-year contract extension as England head coach») Sebastian Gollnow/dpa England head coach Sarina Wiegman will lead the Lionesses through to the end of the 2029 European Women’s Championship after signing a two-year contract extension. Wiegman has guided England to triumphs at the 2022 and 2025 Euros, as well as a first World Cup final in 2023, since taking charge in September 2021. The 56-year-old Dutchwoman, a five-time FIFA Best winner, has reached five successive major tournament finals, also winning the 2017 Euros with her native Netherlands. Wiegman said: “I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football. “Working for a world-class organization, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day. “I am grateful to Mark Bullingham, Debbie Hewitt and the FA board for the incredible way they have backed me, my coaches and support team and, of course, the players. “I am honoured by their trust, which I never take for granted, and want to keep this great partnership going. I have such a strong desire to see what more we can achieve together with our amazing fans. “I also want to keep supporting the wonderful collaborative work being led by the FA across the women’s game, particularly in developing young players and coaches. “Of course, anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realize their potential in the years to come. “We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year.” England, who were beaten by Spain at the 2023 World Cup final in Australia, will face Ukraine over a two-legged play-off in November and December for a place in next year’s tournament in Brazil. Wiegman’s new deal will also encompass the 2027 Nations League, which serves as a qualifying tournament for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. It is the second time she has prolonged her stay in England, having first agreed a contract extension in January 2024. FA CEO Mark Bullingham said: “Sarina is an incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments and I am so happy to continue to work with her for the next Euro cycle. “While we will all remember the trophies and thrilling moments she has given us, I know she is only looking forward. There is no one better to lead the Lionesses into the next two tournaments. “Sarina’s impact on English football has been immense, and she continues to inspire so many throughout the game. We have so much more to do in the women’s game and she will be instrumental in helping us to achieve that.”

item.title: (Video): Patient rotated PSG score 3 goals late to beat talented Strasbourg
item.description: (Video): Patient rotated PSG score 3 goals late to beat talented Strasbourg A rotated PSG side left it late to come back against Strasbourg in an exciting game on Saturday evening in Alsace. If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. PSG came back with a late triple to beat Strasbourg away in Alsace on Saturday afternoon. Gio Reyna fired a shot at the near post which got a crucial touch off a defender to take it past Matvey Safonov in the PSG goal. The game could have changed when Strasbourg had their big chance after the break. Conrad Harder got up well and put in a brilliant header which Safonov saved, and Reyna lashed the follow up over. Harder had another go with 66 minutes on the clock from a tight angle, but the Russian stopper denied him again to keep it at 1-0. Patient PSG win it late Ousmane Dembele celebrates against Strasbourg. Not long after that, everything changed. PSG got lucky with a penalty from nowhere which Ousmane Dembele missed, but with 76 minutes on the clock he swung in a great cross which Ilya Zabarnyi turned in. With 85 minutes played, Dembele got his foot to a loose ball for his first Ligue 1 goal of the season with a nice strike from range. PSG wrapped up the win when Ferran Torres assisted Desire Doue in injury time. You can see the highlights in the clip embedded here: In other news… Luis Enrique changed his team heavily for the game, and it almost backfired. But in the end PSG get the points and a rest for some key starters. Marquinhos was not in the team to face Strasbourg as Luis Enrique continued his strict rotation policy. Maghnes Akliouche got the start – and his manager is delighted with his progress.

item.title: OKC Thunder stat predictions for every player in 2026-27 NBA season
item.description: After bringing virtually everyone back last summer, the OKC Thunder made several changes to its roster this time around. Lu Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins have been traded away. All three helped OKC win a 2025 NBA championship , and their departures will create new opportunities for those still on the team. Cason Wallace figures to take on a starting role. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain will be tasked with providing a scoring punch. And the Thunder will also integrate rookies Aday Mara , Bennett Stirtz , Otega Oweh and Josh Dix . Here are stat predictions for every Thunder player this NBA season : OKC Thunder schedule release 2026-27: See all 82 NBA game times, TV channels OKC Thunder stat predictions for 2026-27 NBA season Points (PTS); Rebounds (REB); Assists (AST); Blocks (BLK); Steals (STL); Personal Fouls (PF); Turnovers (TO); Field Goal Percentage (FG%); 3-Point Percentage (3P%); Free-Throw Percentage (FT%); Minutes (MIN); Games Played (GP) ; Games Started (GS) Brooks Barnhizer 2025-26 stats: 1.7 PTS; 2.0 REB; 0.6 AST; 0.1 BLK; 0.3 STL; 0.7 PF; 0.3 TO; 38.0 FG%; 29.2 3P%; 70.0 FT%; 8.7 MIN; 40 GP; 0 GS Projected 2026-27 stats: 2.0 PTS; 2.2 REB; 0.5 AST; 0.1 BLK; 0.3 STL; 0.8 TO; 40.2 FG%; 31.0 3P%; 71.5 FT%; 9.0 MIN; 35 GP; 0 GS Barnhizer played in 40 games last season, just 10 shy of the maximum games someone can play while on a two-way contract. OKC mostly turned to the then-rookie forward when it was short-handed due to injuries or down the stretch of its blowout victories. Barnhizer has more size than some of OKC's other wings, so that could help him get his number called this season. He also rebounds well and provides plenty of hustle plays. But his struggles from 3-point range ultimately limit how much he can be on the floor. He'll still provide versatility on defense, some catch-and-shoot 3-pointers and a ton of hustle plays. Caruso will also continue to come off the bench and play around 20 minutes per game during the regular season. That's the sweet spot for the 32-year-old guard, who saves his best basketball for the playoffs . But I do expect him to be more efficient this time around after shooting a career-low 29.3% from deep. He's a 6-foot-5 guard who shot 38.4% from distance throughout his four-year college career. That floor spacing could be useful if the Thunder finds itself bitten by the injury bug again. But if that doesn't happen, Dix is likely to spend most of his rookie season with the OKC Blue. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 2025-26 stats: 31.1 PTS; 4.3 REB; 6.6 AST; 0.8 BLK; 1.4 STL; 2.0 PF; 2.2 TO; 55.3 FG%; 38.6 3P%; 87.9 FT%; 33.2 MIN; 68 GP; 68 GS Projected 2026-27 stats: 32.2 PTS; 4.4 REB; 6.1 AST; 0.9 BLK; 1.3 STL; 2.1 PF; 2.3 TO; 54.7 FG%; 40.0 3P%; 90.3 FT%; 34.9 MIN; 76 GP; 76 GS Gilgeous-Alexander only played an average of 6.8 minutes per fourth quarter last season, and he sat out 26 fourth quarters entirely. But I expect the Thunder to be in more close regular-season games this time around since growing pains are to be expected after shaking up the roster. That's why I'm projecting Gilgeous-Alexander to average more points this season despite Jalen Williams , another elite scorer, now being healthy. And I believe he'll become just the 10th different player in NBA history to shoot at least 50% from the field, 40% from deep and 90% from the free-throw line in the same season. Isaiah Hartenstein 2025-26 stats: 9.2 PTS; 9.4 REB; 3.5 AST; 0.8 BLK; 1.0 STL; 2.5 PF; 1.7 TO; 62.2 FG%; 0.0 3P%; 61.0 FT%; 24.2 MIN; 47 GP; 46 GS Projected 2026-27 stats: 8.9 PTS; 9.0 REB; 3.3 AST; 0.9 BLK; 0.7 STL; 2.5 PF; 1.4 TO; 62.9 FG%; 20.0 3P%; 66.4 FT%; 24.0 MIN; 62 GP; 62 GS Jaylin Williams continues to improve his game. Mara looks ready for real minutes after a stellar preseason. And there's still Thomas Sorber , a talented rookie who has yet to make his NBA debut due to injuries. OKC has plenty of center options behind Hartenstein, so it makes sense that his counting stats will decrease a bit, but he'll still be just as impactful. His combination of rebounding, screen setting, passing and rim protecting makes him one of the most valuable contributors on the team. Chet Holmgren 2025-26 stats: 17.1 PTS; 8.9 REB; 1.7 AST; 1.9 BLK; 0.6 STL; 2.3 PF; 1.6 TO; 55.7 FG%; 36.2 3P%; 79.2 FT%; 28.9 MIN; 69 GP; 69 GS Projected 2026-27 stats: 18.2 PTS; 8.6 REB; 1.9 AST; 1.8 BLK; 0.6 STL; 2.3 PF; 1.7 TO; 54.2 FG%; 36.9 3P%; 80.0 FT%; 29.5 MIN; 74 GP; 74 GS Holmgren earned All-NBA third team , All-Defensive first team and All-Star selections last season at age 24. But he still enters this year with something to prove after underperforming against San Antonio in the Western Conference finals . Holmgren's elite work ethic gives me the confidence that he'll bounce back. It'll also help to have a healthy Jalen Williams, who does a great job of finding OKC's bigs for easy buckets, in the mix. Holmgren is a lock to make the All-Defensive team if he meets the requirement for games played, and he should be in the All-NBA and All-Star conversations once again. More: Who will be OKC Thunder's biggest threats other than Wemby, Spurs? Let's rank them Aday Mara 2025-26 stats: None Projected 2026-27 stats: 6.8 PTS; 5.1 REB; 1.7 AST; 1.2 BLK; 0.2 STL; 1.8 PF; 0.9 TO; 63.4 FG%; 12.5 3P%; 67.9 FT%; 14.6 MIN; 66 GP; 3 GS Mara absolutely dominated during the preseason. The 7-3, 262 pound center was rim deterrent for opposing players. He was a lob threat for his teammates. He was a force on the boards. And he was a skilled passer at his size. But most impressively, Mara made significant improvements to his conditioning after it was a clear weakness during college and Summer League play. He showed that he's ready for real minutes, and he should get them this season despite being in a crowded frontcourt. Jared McCain 2025-26 stats: 8.3 PTS; 2.0 REB; 1.3 AST; 0.1 BLK; 0.5 STL; 1.2 PF; 0.8 TO; 42.5 FG%; 38.5 3P%; 86.4 FT%; 17.3 MIN; 67 GP; 3 GS Projected 2026-27 stats: 12.1 PTS; 2.3 REB; 2.2 AST; 0.1 BLK; 0.7 STL; 1.5 PF; 1.1 TO; 47.1 FG%; 40.4 3P%; 86.8 FT%; 23.1 MIN; 72 GP; 1 GS It isn't easy to join a championship contender at the trade deadline and get thrown into a key role, but McCain did exactly that last season. The former Philadelphia guard provided a spark off the bench for OKC and even started in two playoff games. McCain now has even more familiarity with the Thunder's system, and he'll have even more opportunities with Joe and Wiggins no longer around. item.title: At Strasbourg, Gio Reyna is starting to gain what had been elusive: momentum
item.description: A goal against PSG is proof on the scoresheet of what can be seen on the teamsheet: At long last, Reyna is getting consistent minutes. For an entire four-year cycle, to write about Gio Reyna was to write about his potential – especially the nagging feeling that it was going unfulfilled. Once hyped as possibly the greatest prospect in US men’s history, a series of injuries kept him from simply taking the field, much less making his mark on it. Since his emergent 2020-21 season, when he logged nearly 2,000 Bundesliga minutes running alongside Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, and Jadon Sancho, Reyna finished each of the ensuing five seasons without even cresting 630 league minutes. “Rotational” became a generous descriptor for his role at Nottingham Forest on loan, and then last season with Borussia Mönchengladbach. Still, Gregg Berhalter and Mauricio Pochettino kept involving Reyna with the US squad based on that pesky potential – betting that, on his day, he still had the raw talent to do what few compatriots could. Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Another unremarkable win shows Arsenal’s strength is in depth rather than creativity | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Champions so risk-averse Forest were lured into thinking they had a chance, until bench was used to see them off Pass. Pass. Pass. Pass. Sideways. Square. Backwards. Pass. Pass. Recycle. Pass. It wasn’t much of a spectacle. But in the end, for the second week running, thanks in no small part of their bench, Arsenal won. Fireworks in the autumn are for Bonfire Night; titles require relentless accumulation. Since the international break, Arsenal have won three games out of three despite not being in the lead at half-time in any of them. Hammered at Brighton and having endured a drab first hour at home to Leeds last week, there has been a rare sense, for the first time really since Manchester City dropped points at Everton at the beginning of May, of Arsenal not being quite at their best, needing to reassert their quality. This was not a performance that would terrify any opponent, but it did highlight Arsenal’s consistency and it did demonstrate just how deep their squad now runs. Continue reading...

item.title: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace
item.description: At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season. Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool | Sid Lowe
item.description: It will be a tense time for Europe’s longest serving president, despite the Champions League game at Anfield offering a symbol of how far they have come The first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half empty. It was a Sunday night in the second division, they lost 3-0 against Badajoz, and he didn’t enjoy it much. But then, he never enjoys it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous,” he says. “It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious. I suffer a lot. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manzambi maintains Aston Villa progress with win to seal dismal week for Newcastle
item.description: There is a reason why Aston Villa were so desperate to hijack Johan Manzambi’s proposed summer move from Freiburg to Newcastle. The tall, quick, tricky, clever and perfectly balanced 21-year-old Switzerland attacking midfielder looked worth every penny of the record £50m plus fee Villa ended up paying and he duly delighted in showing Tynesiders what they missed. For Newcastle and their disconsolate manager, Matthias Jaissle, there was a cruel irony that Manzambi ended up heading the winner on a day when the Premier League’s CEO, Richard Masters, was in the directors’ box to watch arguably the two teams most affected by the spending rules imposed during his tenure. Continue reading...

item.title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
item.description: There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games. Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules . Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear, albeit with a few scares between, courtesy of Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming. Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produce Some criticism has been OTT and a fee rising to £116m heightens demands but, yes, compared with his performances in Germany and for Germany Wirtz has underwhelmed at Liverpool. The past week has encapsulated his Liverpool career so far. In the Champions League rout of Lask he was everywhere, exploiting gaps between and behind the Austrian club’s defence and knitting together a dominant display against limited opposition. In the previous game against Manchester City , however, when Andoni Iraola needed big players to step up in the absence of Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, Wirtz was ineffective, wasteful and withdrawn when his team were chasing the game at 0-1. It also did not help his cause that Rayan Cherki, a cheaper alternative whom Liverpool considered and passed on, completed City’s victory with a sublime goal. AH Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
item.description: This is by far the most interesting this club have ever been and they faced PSG, a kind of twin entity in all this as oil state glove puppets Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash. In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals , a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade Paris Saint-Germain team. Continue reading...

item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Continue reading...

item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals , but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season ,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000 . But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties. Continue reading...

item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Sliding Doors meets Biff’s Almanac: City saga stirs up a world of alternate histories | Max Rushden
item.description: Even New Romantics have a view but this long story will not be cut short amid endless hypotheticals and split narratives It’s Wednesday afternoon (UK time) and I find myself interviewing Tony Hadley on TalkSport about his upcoming big band tour. We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...
